commits.pr_title: [Transformers backend] Serve Qwen2 with the Transformers modeling backend
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->
## Overview

Serve Qwen2 with the Transformers modeling backend. Native `vllm/model_executor/models/qwen2.py` is deleted; models that still build natively use the Qwen3 classes configured for Qwen2 attention. Tracked in #67003.

## Claims

- `Qwen2ForCausalLM` and `Qwen2Model` checkpoints resolve to the Transformers modeling backend.
- Native Qwen3 owns the decoder stack: `Qwen3MLP` and `Qwen3Model` are the former Qwen2 implementations, `Qwen3Attention` makes q/k-norm optional, and `Qwen3ForCausalLM` gains `SupportsQuant` and reads `get_text_config()`.
- `use_qwen2_attention(config)` sets `attention_bias=True` and leaves q/k-norm off unless the config enables it, so Qwen3 classes build Qwen2's attention. MiMo, MiMo-MTP and the Qwen2 reward models use it; DomynEdge and Qwen3-DFlash import Qwen3 classes directly.
- `init_vllm_registered_model` builds an inner `Qwen2ForCausalLM` (Qwen2-VL, Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen2-Audio, Qwen2.5-Omni, Kimi-Audio, MiniCPM-V 2.6, FireRedASR2, MiDashengLM, dots.ocr, AudioFlamingo3, Bagel, OpenCUA, ...) as native `Qwen3ForCausalLM` with Qwen2 attention, so composite models keep their native text model and `language_model.model(...)` calls unchanged.

## Gaps

- [x] #66833
  - Qwen2-VL and Qwen2.5-VL produce wrong output with CUDA graphs: the M-RoPE positions were a fresh copy each step outside the compiled region. Also affects backend multimodal M-RoPE models on `main`.
- [x] #65446
  - gte-Qwen2 (`is_causal: false`) fails to compile: the cudagraph buffer-assignment check rejects a `dict.update` in the traced forward
- [x] #66819
  - `DomynEdgeForCausalLM` fails `test_initialization` (native sliding-window assertion), also on `main`
- [x] #66834
  - Dual-chunk attention (`dual_chunk_attention_config`, Qwen2.5-7B/14B-Instruct-1M) has no backend equivalent, but isn't a regression: its attention backend was removed in #25351 and the leftover plumbing makes these checkpoints fail on `main`
- [x] #65965
  - Quark checkpoints with `{k,v}_proj.output_scale` fail to load: the QKV fuser renames them before Quark's rule matches
- [x] #67455
  - `Qwen2Model` embedding models without a sentence-transformers config default to CLS pooling instead of LAST
  - Bidirectional Qwen2 embedding models (gte-Qwen2, `is_causal: false`) run causal attention on the backend, because HF's Qwen2 attention hardcodes `is_causal`
- [x] vllm-project/vllm-gguf-plugin#154 and a plugin release with vllm-project/vllm-gguf-plugin#149
  - GGUF fails to load: the plugin's linear assumes 2D activations and the tied `lm_head` has no `bias`. With both: Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct Q6_K GSM8K native 0.596, backend 0.604

## Validation

B200, `main` ce72586f8a (native) vs this branch. Throughput is `vllm bench throughput` 1024 in / 256 out x 1000 prompts; latency is batch 1, 128 in / 256 out. Models that take the Transformers modeling backend:

| | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct throughput (req/s, 3 runs) | 59.03 / 58.91 / 59.02 | 59.33 / 59.27 / 59.33 |
| Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct latency | 0.877 s | 0.872 s |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct throughput, 5000 prompts (req/s, 3 runs) | 157.8 / 139.1 / 168.2 | 171.5 / 168.3 / 150.9 |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct latency | 0.424 s | 0.408 s |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct GSM8K | 0.538 | 0.550 |

Native models this PR rebuilds on the Qwen3 classes:

| | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B GSM8K | 0.884 | 0.887 |
| Qwen3-8B online FP8 GSM8K (`SupportsQuant`) | 0.880 | 0.882 |
| MiMo-7B-RL + MiMo MTP GSM8K, acceptance rate | 0.794, 0.906 | 0.795, 0.906 |
| Qwen3-4B + DFlash drafter, DomynEdge-SFT (greedy, 3 prompts) | | identical |
| Qwen2-VL-2B ChartQA | 0.602 | 0.600 |
| MiniCPM-V 2.6 ChartQA | 0.650 | 0.654 |
| Qwen2.5-VL-3B ChartQA | 0.678 | 0.680 |
| InternVL2-1B ChartQA | 0.574 | 0.574 |
| Qwen2.5-Omni-3B ChartQA | 0.690 | 0.688 |
| LLaVA-OneVision-0.5B ChartQA | 0.458 | 0.458 |
| Qwen2-Audio-7B LibriSpeech WER | 0.080 | 0.081 |
| Qwen2.5-Omni-3B LibriSpeech WER | 0.048 | 0.048 |

The B200 was shared during these runs: CPU-bound Qwen2.5-1.5B throughput varies ±15% run to run with no consistent direction, Qwen2.5-7B is stable. GSM8K is 1319 questions, 5-shot, ±1.3 pt noise. ChartQA is the first 500 test questions (relaxed accuracy), LibriSpeech is the first 500 test-clean clips. FireRedASR2 (`embed_input_ids` now requires `is_multimodal`) and Kimi-Audio (32 audio tower `qkv_proj.bias.k` weights not loaded) fail at startup on `main` and the branch alike.

```bash
vllm bench throughput --model <model> --input-len 1024 --output-len 256 --num-prompts 1000 --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune": false}'
vllm bench latency --model <model> --batch-size 1 --input-len 128 --output-len 256
vllm serve <model> --max-model-len 4096 [--quantization fp8 | --speculative-config '{"method": "mimo_mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 1}']
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py
```

`test_initialization` for the Qwen2 architectures, every model file this PR touches and Qwen3/DFlash (51 architectures): 50 passed, 3 skipped, 1 failed, identical on `main` (Qwen2.5-Omni-7B-AWQ's AWQ PTX doesn't load on this host's CUDA 13.0 driver). Tensorized Qwen2.5-1.5B files load across implementations (#67205). Fusion e2e and `test_backend` use no Qwen2 models.

No open PR duplicates this (searched for Qwen2 and the Transformers modeling backend; #60648 and #57315 are related).

commits.pr_title: [CI] Bump Transformers version to 5.23.0
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Bump Transformers to [v5.23.0](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/releases/tag/v5.23.0). Follows https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64529.

## Claims

- `requirements/common.txt` allows `transformers >= 5.16.1, < 5.24.0`, and CI pins 5.23.0.
- Breaking changes in 5.23 (`ep_router` removal huggingface/transformers#49615, exporters, Wav2Vec2ProcessorWithLM, serve) do not touch vLLM.
- Base processors now check that placeholder counts match the media passed (huggingface/transformers#49976). vLLM always calls them with dummy text built from the item counts (`_get_hf_mm_inputs`), so this should only hit models that override that path.
- InternLM3 and IQuestCoder are now native in Transformers. vLLM already maps both to `LlamaForCausalLM`, and the native InternLM3 config exposes `attention_bias`/`mlp_bias`, which `llama.py` reads.
- The transcription tests gated on `5.23.0.dev0` (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65735) now run in CI.

## Validation

The HF PyPI mirror does not have 5.23.0 yet, so the compiled requirements were edited by hand (pin and hashes from pypi.org, committed with `SKIP=pip-compile`) and this is validated by `/ci run nightly`. Results to follow.

commits.pr_title: [MM] Support mm_device_do_normalize for LLaVA-OneVision
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Enables `mm_device_do_normalize` for LLaVA-OneVision, following #64487 (Gemma 3) and #66690 (Qwen2.5-Omni).

## Claims

- LLaVA-OneVision supports `mm_device_do_normalize`, on by default; the docs table lists it.
- Accuracy is unchanged.
- Bee and R-4B, which subclass the model, keep CPU-side normalisation.

## Validation

Single CUDA GPU, `main` at a9dcfae9e, `llava-hf/llava-onevision-qwen2-0.5b-ov-hf`, fp16.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| New `test_mm_device_do_normalize` (image + video) | PR: 1 passed. Base: 1 failed (flag resolves to False) |
| `generation/test_common.py -k llava_onevision` (HF comparison) | 2 passed |
| llava-bench PPL, flag off / on / Transformers | 11.4485 / 11.4485 / 11.4593 (−0.09%) |
| Greedy outputs, flag on vs off (12 image + 4 video requests) | 16/16 identical |
| `test_initialization.py` for OneVision, Bee, R-4B | passed |

```bash
pytest -v tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_llava_onevision.py -k test_mm_device_do_normalize
pytest -v tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_common.py -k llava_onevision
```

PPL uses `vqa_ppl_test` through a small wrapper, not a new `generation_ppl_test/` entry: the helper fixes `max_model_len=4096`, too small for this model's image tokens, and passes the answer as a plain string, which this model's chat template drops.

<details>
<summary>PPL wrapper</summary>

```python
import pytest

from tests.models.utils import GenerateModelInfo

from . import ppl_utils


@pytest.mark.parametrize("mm_device_do_normalize", [False, True])
def test_ppl(hf_runner, vllm_runner, monkeypatch, mm_device_do_normalize: bool):
    def runner(name, **kwargs):
        kwargs["max_model_len"] = 16384
        return vllm_runner(name, **kwargs)

    from_pretrained = ppl_utils.AutoProcessor.from_pretrained

    def patched(*args, **kwargs):
        proc = from_pretrained(*args, **kwargs)
        apply = proc.apply_chat_template

        def apply_chat_template(conv, **kw):
            conv = [
                {**m, "content": [{"type": "text", "text": m["content"]}]}
                if isinstance(m["content"], str)
                else m
                for m in conv
            ]
            return apply(conv, **kw)

        proc.apply_chat_template = apply_chat_template
        return proc

    monkeypatch.setattr(ppl_utils.AutoProcessor, "from_pretrained", patched)

    ppl_utils.vqa_ppl_test(
        hf_runner,
        runner,
        GenerateModelInfo("llava-hf/llava-onevision-qwen2-0.5b-ov-hf"),
        vllm_extra_kwargs={"mm_device_do_normalize": mm_device_do_normalize},
    )
```
</details>

## Details

- The norm runs in the model, just before the tower, as in `nemotron_vl.py`. `init_vision_tower_for_llava` can also return CLIP or Pixtral, which take no `input_norm`.
- Bee and R-4B opt out because I did not validate them. With the flag off the norm is only a dtype cast, so they do not change.
- Not measured: preprocessing throughput. Not tested: larger checkpoints, ROCm, XPU.
- No duplicate found in PRs, issues or comments. #57379 edits the same file but not normalisation.
- AI assistance was used in this PR.

commits.pr_title: [MM] Support mm_device_do_normalize for Qwen3-Omni
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Enables `mm_device_do_normalize` for Qwen3-Omni, so image and video pixels are sent as `uint8` and rescaled/normalised on the GPU, as Qwen3-VL already does. Follow-up to #66690 (Qwen2.5-Omni), whose mixin change Qwen3-Omni already inherits.

## Claims

- Qwen3-Omni now supports `mm_device_do_normalize`, on by default like the other supported models; the docs table lists it.
- Accuracy is unchanged: llava-bench PPL is 7.4409 with the flag on and off (Transformers 7.4316, +0.12%), and greedy outputs on four image/video requests are token-identical with the flag on and off.

## Validation

1x H200, `main` at 329f93e19, `Qwen/Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct`, bf16.

**PPL test** (new `Qwen/Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct` entry in `generation_ppl_test/test_qwen.py`, llava-bench-in-the-wild, 60 images, factor 32):

| `mm_device_do_normalize` | vLLM PPL | Transformers PPL | Difference |
|---|---|---|---|
| False | 7.4409 | 7.4316 | +0.12% |
| True | 7.4409 | 7.4316 | +0.12% |

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/models/multimodal/generation_ppl_test/test_qwen.py -k model_info4
# 1x H200: 2 passed
# GPU < 120 GB: 2 skipped ("Need at least 120GB GPU memory")
```

The entry is marked `large_gpu_mark(min_gb=120)`: `vqa_ppl_test` runs vLLM at `gpu_memory_utilization=0.7`, and the bf16 checkpoint is ~66 GB, so it is skipped on the 35 GB MIG slice of the PPL CI step and on 80 GB cards. `hf_ppl` is a constant computed once with `Qwen3OmniMoeForConditionalGeneration(...).thinker` using the same prompts, processor kwargs and loss masking as `ppl_utils` (whose `AutoModelForImageTextToText` does not cover the Omni checkpoint), as in #66690.

Note: this test cannot fail on the base commit, because there the flag resolves to `False` (checked with the earlier processor test), so both cases run the CPU path. What shows the fix is the run above printing `mm_device_do_normalize: True` with the same PPL.

**Greedy outputs, flag on vs off** (4 requests: two single images, a two-image comparison, a video; 96 tokens; runs interleaved off/on/off/on): all four requests are token-identical across all runs, with identical top-1 logprobs.

```bash
pre-commit run --from-ref HEAD~2 --to-ref HEAD   # all pass, incl. mypy
```

## Details

**Why it was off.** `Qwen3Omni_VisionTransformer` is its own class (not `Qwen3_VisionTransformer`), and it took no `input_norm`; `Qwen3OmniMoeThinkerForConditionalGeneration` did not set `supports_mm_device_do_normalize`, so the flag resolved to `False`.

**Change.** Mirror Qwen3-VL: the vision tower takes an optional `input_norm` (default `IdentityInputNorm`) and calls it in `forward` in place of the `.to(dtype=self.dtype)` cast; the thinker passes `build_mm_input_norm(vllm_config.model_config)` and sets the class flag. The image/video `_process_*_input` methods come from `Qwen2_5OmniConditionalGenerationMixin`, which no longer pre-casts `pixel_values` since #66690, so no change is needed there. Norm parameters come from the flat `preprocessor_config.json`, which `_load_norm_params` already reads.

**Limits.** Not measured: preprocessing throughput or PCIe savings. Not tested: `use_audio_in_video`, the Thinking checkpoint (same architecture), ROCm/XPU (the kernel and its CPU fallback are shared with Qwen3-VL).

**Duplicates and related PRs.** None found (`gh search prs` for `mm_device_do_normalize`, `gh pr list` for Qwen3-Omni). #63809 (ViT full CUDA graph for Qwen3-Omni, open) edits the same vision tower and builds its capture `dummy_pixel_values` with the model dtype; if both land, the capture input should use `self.visual.input_norm.input_dtype or dtype` like Qwen3-VL. Happy to rebase on it, or adjust it, whichever lands second.

**AI assistance.** Claude Code wrote the change and tests, ran the H200 validation and drafted this text. I reviewed every changed line and ran the commands above.

---

commits.pr_title: [CI][Test] Run test_mm_prefix_lm_pipeline_parallel with spawned workers
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`(L4) Distributed Models` Shard 2/4 has failed on nearly every main build since [102677](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/102677): 12 final failures through 102765, plus nightly 102740. The original runs and their retries fail the same way:

```
models/multimodal/generation/test_mm_prefix_lm.py::test_mm_prefix_lm_pipeline_parallel
(Worker pid=5479) ... gpu_worker.py:514 init_device
RuntimeError: Cannot re-initialize CUDA in forked subprocess. To use CUDA with multiprocessing, you must use the 'spawn' start method
E RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above. Failed core proc(s): {'EngineCore': 1}
```

The test (added in #65996) forks its EngineCore and worker. When its auto-shard also collects tests that initialize CUDA during collection, the forked worker inherits that CUDA state and can't initialize. The failing runs collect 336–339 items, including `test_phi4mm.py`, whose module-level `snapshot_download` runs at collection time. Runs that collect a different set pass. The test fails only in that L4 shard, and the AMD mirror passes.

This sets `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn` for the test, the same fix (and comment) that `test_maverick`, `test_dots_ocr`, `test_unlimited_ocr`, `test_whisper` and `test_transformers_{video,audio}` in this suite already use. It's a test-only change. Which collected module initializes CUDA in the pytest parent isn't pinned down; that would be a separate hardening.

## Not a duplicate

I searched open PRs for `test_mm_prefix_lm` and "re-initialize CUDA forked". No results, and no revert of #65996.

## Test Plan

- CI: `distributed-model-tests-2-gpus` (L4, auto-sharded), as a selected-steps build on this PR.
- `pre-commit run --files tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_mm_prefix_lm.py`

## Test Result

- pre-commit passes.
- GPU: [build 102773](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/102773), `distributed-model-tests-2-gpus` (L4): all 4 shards passed. `test_mm_prefix_lm_pipeline_parallel` ran in Shard 2/4 with 336 other tests deselected, the same collection that failed on main, and passed.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; I reviewed the change.

commits.pr_body:
The test uses images resized to at most 384×384, but profiling still uses the model’s maximum image size. This requires a 256 GiB attention matrix with FP32 SDPA’s math backend on XPU; CUDA’s memory-efficient backend avoids this allocation.

Bound profiling to the test’s image dimensions, leaving `max_num_seqs`, graph-capture settings, and exact output assertions unchanged.

commits.pr_title: [Perf] Allow EPLB with modular TRT-LLM FP8 block-scale MoE
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`TrtLlmFp8ExpertsModular._supports_parallel_config` rejects `enable_eplb`. The gate came in with the MoE refactor vllm-project/vllm#32564 ("[MoE Refactor] Create MK for TRTLLM Kernels"). It has no comment, issue or error report. It matches the monolithic class, which routes inside the kernel and so only supports naive DP/EP and TP. The modular class does not route itself: it takes the router's EPLB-mapped physical expert ids, with `num_experts` / `local_expert_offset` in physical units. Its BlockMajorK weights and block scales stay expert-major, so EPLB's per-expert dim-0 moves are valid.

This PR drops the EPLB rejection from the modular class. The monolithic class keeps its rejection.

## Test Plan

- GLM-5.3 FP8, DEP8 on 2x4 GB300, `--all2all-backend flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided`, `--enable-eplb` with the sync pynccl communicator, 16 or 32 redundant experts.
- Agentic rollout benchmark: ~30k input / 6k output tokens, 24 turns, GRPO n=8, 65k context, 64 groups.
- Correctness: GSM8K (n=123, greedy) before and after a KV-cache flood.

## Test Result

| arm | tok/s/GPU | EPLB balancedness |
|---|---|---|
| no EPLB | 722 | 0.58 |
| EPLB, 32 redundant | 804-806 (+11.6%) | ~0.95 |
| EPLB, 16 redundant | 804 | ~0.95 |

- The gain held across 16 and 32 redundant experts and across rebalance step intervals of 1000 and 3000.
- GSM8K stayed within run-to-run noise (.90-.95).
- Async EPLB over NIXL hung cross-node in our setup, so these runs used the sync pynccl communicator.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][AuxOutput] Size the routed-experts row cache from one source
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

The routed-experts row cache is sized in two places that disagree:

- The scheduler (`AuxOutputSchedulerConnector._capacity`) keeps `num_blocks` KV blocks of rows, doubled when a KV connector is configured, and ignores `aux_output_config.max_bytes`.
- The worker store (`initialize_output_storage`) uses `max_bytes` when set, otherwise `num_blocks * hashes_per_kv_block` objects, with no KV-connector doubling.

So setting `max_bytes` only changed the worker: the scheduler still retained (and kept serving prefix hits for) as many blocks as the KV cache, and the worker store grew past `max_bytes` to hold them. With a KV connector and no `max_bytes`, the scheduler retained twice what the worker allocated.

This PR adds `retained_objects(vllm_config, kv_cache_config)` as the single source for both sides. The scheduler capacity and the worker `max_bytes` are both derived from it. The routed-experts dtype and bytes-per-token computation are also shared (`get_routed_experts_bytes_per_token`), so the worker and the capacity computation cannot drift.

Behavior changes:

- `max_bytes` set: the scheduler now retains at most `max_bytes // object_nbytes` hash-block objects (at least one).
- No `max_bytes`, KV connector configured: the worker store now matches the scheduler's 2x.
- No `max_bytes`, no KV connector: unchanged.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/distributed/aux_output_connector tests/config/test_aux_output_config.py tests/model_executor/test_routed_experts_capture.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py
```

`test_retained_objects_follow_max_bytes` covers the KV-cache default, the KV-connector doubling, `max_bytes`, and the one-object floor.

## Test Result

523 passed. The new test fails to import on main (`retained_objects` does not exist there).

commits.pr_title: [Model] Remove OpenPangu-VL
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Remove `OpenPanguVLForConditionalGeneration`, which cannot start on any vLLM release that requires Transformers v5 (v0.24.0 onwards).

If accepted, close these open PRs that only fix removed OpenPangu-VL code:

- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56390 (`openpangu` video loader `num_frames=-1` crash)

## Claims

- `FreedomIntelligence/openPangu-VL-7B` fails at engine startup on `main` and on v0.31.0, including image-only, because its remote processor code is incompatible with Transformers v5.
- The architecture is added to `_PREVIOUSLY_SUPPORTED_MODELS` with v0.23.0, the last release with Transformers v4 and the last one where it starts.
- The VL-only `openpangu` video loader and interleaved M-RoPE (`MRotaryEmbeddingInterleaved`, the `"openpangu"` RoPE type) go with it. The text-only openPangu models are unaffected.

## Validation

`vllm serve FreedomIntelligence/openPangu-VL-7B --trust-remote-code --max-model-len 8192` on B200:

| vLLM | Transformers | Default | `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"video": 0}'` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` (ce72586f8) | 5.22.2 | ❌ `ImportError: cannot import name 'BASE_VIDEO_PROCESSOR_DOCSTRING'` | ❌ same |
| v0.31.0 | 5.14.1 | ❌ `StrictDataclassFieldValidationError` on video `do_convert_rgb` | ❌ `'OpenPanguVLImageProcessorFast' object has no attribute 'min_pixels'` |
| v0.23.0 | 4.57.6 | ✅ starts with `--enforce-eager`, answers an image request | |

`main` requires `transformers >= 5.16.1`, and `BASE_VIDEO_PROCESSOR_DOCSTRING` was removed in 5.15, so no supported Transformers version can load it. The test registry has skipped this model on every Transformers v5 since https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/30566, so CI never caught this. No issue reports it, and the later OpenPangu-VL fixes (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55941, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56390) were found by code inspection rather than by users. The checkpoint has 290 downloads in the last 30 days and has not been updated since 2026-01-17. The open https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56390 only touches the deleted video loader.

Patches tried before removing it, each of which only exposed the next incompatibility:

- https://huggingface.co/FreedomIntelligence/openPangu-VL-7B/discussions/2 adds `total=False` to `OpenPanguVLVideoProcessorInitKwargs` in the remote code. It has been open since 2026-02-11 without a response, and it does not touch the import or signature problems below.
- Setting `total=False` on remote code kwargs `TypedDict`s at import time (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/67502) fixes the kwargs validation, then startup fails on the `BASE_VIDEO_PROCESSOR_DOCSTRING` import.
- Aliasing `transformers.video_processing_utils.BASE_VIDEO_PROCESSOR_DOCSTRING = ""` in `vllm/transformers_utils/processor.py` fixes the import, then video preprocessing fails with `TypeError: OpenPanguVLVideoProcessor._preprocess() missing 2 required positional arguments: 'do_convert_rgb' and 'interpolation'`, because Transformers v5 passes `resample` and consumes `do_convert_rgb` earlier.
- With video disabled on v0.31.0 (Transformers 5.14.1, where the import still works), the remote image processor also fails (`'OpenPanguVLImageProcessorFast' object has no attribute 'min_pixels'`), so image-only serving is no workaround.

Fixing the remaining signature and attribute errors from vLLM would mean overriding this one model's processor methods, so it is better fixed in the checkpoint or by adding the model to Transformers.

Tests (B200): `tests/models/test_registry.py` 454 passed; `tests/kernels/core/` rotary/M-RoPE tests 418 passed; `tests/multimodal/test_video.py` has the same 11 torchcodec failures as `main` (environment) and one fewer test (the removed `openpangu` case); `openPangu-Embedded-1B-V1.1` generates identically to `main`.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Bugfix][RL] Fix sparse NCCL update OOM and improve performance
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Problems with `sparse_nccl` on main:

- **Memory:** a worker keeps every patch on the GPU until the last one arrives, 6 bytes per changed element on every rank whatever the TP size. On the default config the extensible KV cache leaves about 3 GiB free, so a one-shot `send_weights` on Qwen3-30B-A3B at TP4 fails at 1.25% of elements changed, after some weights are already written.
- **Time:** each tensor costs two allocations and two broadcasts, 37,734 per update on this model, and the `empty_cache` at the end of the update then releases thousands of cached blocks. At 3% changed these take 2.2 s of a 4.3 s update.
- **Non-contiguous patch tensors** are broadcast as they are, so the wrong bytes are sent.

This PR sends the update in batches of at most 512 MiB. Both ends cut it at the same patches with one `batches()` over the update's metadata, and a patch above the limit forms its own batch.

- **Memory:** the worker applies each batch before receiving the next, so patch memory is bounded by the batch size instead of the update size.
- **Time:** a batch is one broadcast of all its indices plus one of its values per dtype. The worker receives each into one buffer and splits it into per-patch views, so an update takes a few allocations and broadcasts instead of two per tensor, and leaves few cached blocks for `empty_cache`.
- **Non-contiguous tensors:** the trainer concatenates each batch before sending it, so the wire always carries contiguous bytes.

Since a batch is applied before the rest arrive, a worker whose batch fails to validate or load keeps receiving and raises at the end, so the trainer's broadcasts complete and the group stays usable.

## Claims

- On Qwen3-30B-A3B at TP4 on the default config, main fails at 1.25% of elements changed and this passes up to 50%, the highest tested.
- In one engine, batching cuts the update time by 21% / 33% / 50% at 0.1% / 1% / 3% changed, to about 2.1 s at each.
- Broadcasts per update drop from 37,734 to 2-22.
- Weights and outputs match main.

## Validation

Setup: 4×H20 at TP4 with the trainer on a fifth H20, Triton MoE, main `cb59326ae` wheel, torch 2.14.0+cu130. Patches sit at evenly spaced, sorted positions.

```bash
VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B --tensor-parallel-size 4 --moe-backend triton \
  --weight-transfer-config '{"backend": "sparse_nccl"}'
```

Each round: `POST /pause?mode=keep`, `SparseNCCLTrainerWeightTransferEngine.send_weights(patches)`, `POST /resume`.

**Memory limit.** The server above, 2 rounds per density, no client load.

| Elements changed | Sent | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1% | 1.71 GiB | passes | passes |
| 1.25% | 2.13 GiB | `OutOfMemoryError` while staging | passes |
| 3, 5, 10, 15, 20% | 5.1-34.1 GiB | not run | passes |
| 30% | 51.2 GiB | not run | passes |
| 50% | 85.3 GiB | not run | passes |

Peak memory stayed at 94.4-95.6 of 95.6 GiB. The rows up to 20% ran before the one-pass validation was on main; 30% and 50% ran with it.

**Update time in one engine.** `LLM` with the same model and parallelism, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.85`, `enforce_eager=True`, and the one-pass validation in both arms. Time of `send_weights`, median of 6 rounds, arms alternating round by round. The batched arm is a bench copy of this wire that sends each batch in its own `update_weights` call (1, 4 and 11 calls); this PR sends one.

| Elements changed | Sent | main | Batched | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.1% | 0.17 GiB | 2.63 s | 2.08 s | -21% |
| 1% | 1.71 GiB | 3.14 s | 2.11 s | -33% |
| 3% | 5.12 GiB | 4.29 s | 2.14 s | -50% |

Receiving drops from 0.54 / 0.70 / 1.28 s to 0.05-0.06 s, and the final `empty_cache` from 0.04 / 0.29 / 0.88 s to under 10 ms. The other phases don't change.

- **HTTP under load** (`--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85`, 32 streaming clients, 2 servers per arm, 8 rounds, this PR's code without the one-pass validation): the pause drops from 5.04 / 5.55 / 7.24 s to 4.41 / 4.53 / 4.87 s, about the time saved in one engine, and extra GPU memory at 3% from 6.65 to 2.02 GiB.
- **Output:** `/weight_checker` digests of all 1,740 weights and greedy per-token logprobs match main, with zero client errors.
- **Real NCCL** on two GPUs: mixed dtypes, odd counts, one name in two dtypes, an empty patch, a non-contiguous tensor and five batch sizes all land correctly. After a failed batch the trainer gets the error, and the next update works on the same group.
- **Qwen3.5-35B-A3B** (1,811 tensors, packed experts): on the default config, main runs out of memory while receiving at 3% and the trainer stays blocked in NCCL; this passes 20% and 30%. In one engine the update takes 4% / 8% / 12% less, since this model has few tensors. All arms carry a one-line fix, also in an open PR, for a separate bug that leaves NaN in GDN conv1d weights.

**Tests**

```bash
VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION=1 pytest tests/distributed/test_weight_transfer.py -k sparse  # 23 passed, 1 skipped (no GPU)
```

- The three batching cases fail on main, which receives every patch before applying any. The drain case passes on main too, since main also receives everything before it fails.
- All 16 hand-written mutants of the new code fail the new tests.
- The nightly Distributed Features step runs this file. CI can't reproduce the memory limit, which needs this model on GPUs.

<details>
<summary>The new tests on main</summary>

```bash
git checkout origin/main -- vllm/distributed/weight_transfer/sparse_nccl_engine.py
VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION=1 pytest tests/distributed/test_weight_transfer.py -k "wire_batches or failed_batch"
```

```text
E       assert [6, 6] == [2, 4, 6]
E       assert [6, 6] == [2, 4]
E       assert [6, 6] == [3, 3]
3 failed, 1 passed
```

</details>

## Details

**Wire format.** Values go in one run per dtype, in order of first appearance, so input order is kept even when a name repeats in another dtype. The packed helpers don't fit: `unpack_tensor` rejects int32 indices next to BF16 values with odd counts, and a pack can separate a patch's indices from its values.

**Behavior changes**

- Validation is per batch, so an invalid later batch fails after earlier batches landed. The worker stays marked incomplete, and the docs already say to restart or reseed after a partial failure.
- The wire format changes, so the trainer and workers must run the same version. `wire_batch_bytes` in the update info is required, so a mismatched worker rejects the update instead of receiving the wrong layout, though the trainer may already be blocked in a broadcast.
- The trainer concatenates each batch before sending it, so it holds one extra batch: at most 512 MiB, or one larger patch that travels alone.

**Limits.** Two models, TP4, H20 and Triton MoE. Index positions are synthetic. Cross-node transport was not measured.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR batches the sparse NCCL wire. One open PR fixes non-contiguous patches with a narrower change; this one covers that case too.

---

commits.pr_title: [Quantization][MoE] Keep NVFP4 expert scales CSF-compressed on the GPU with B12X
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Keeps the CSF-compressed routed-expert block scales of `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP4-Local` compressed on the GPU when the NVFP4 MoE backend is B12X: -2.57 GiB of weights, +18.7% KV cache on one RTX PRO 6000 Max-Q, +2.4 GiB free memory on DGX Spark, GSM8K unchanged.

Builds on #64312, which decodes CSF scales at load. Loading the checkpoint from the Hub also needs #64739 (shards under `tensors/`).

At load, B12X re-encodes each rank's decoded scales with FlashInfer's `encode_csf_scales` and hands them to b12x as `CsfScalePlanes`; b12x expands only the routed experts' scales per call into one scratch per layer shape. Re-encoding the rank's slice needs no loader change and works for any TP size. The encoder uses the same base rule as the checkpoint, so the streams are as small as the checkpoint's.

- Only B12X with NVFP4 activations keeps scales compressed, and only for layers with `weight_scale_encoding: csf`. Other backends, W4A16 and `csf_32x2_v1` keep #64312's decode at load.
- On by default for `csf` checkpoints, which target memory-bound local devices. `--kernel-config '{"b12x_moe_uncompressed_scales": true}'` restores decode at load with the same kernels.
- Not supported: expert parallelism (B12X is TP-only) and weight reloading of compressed layers (`NotImplementedError`, captured graphs read the first load's storage).

## Results

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP4-Local, MTP-3, B12X, base = main + #64739.

| | DGX Spark (GB10) | RTX PRO 6000 Max-Q (300 W) |
|---|---|---|
| model weights (GiB) | 72.08 -> 69.51 | 72.06 -> 69.49 |
| KV cache | fixed 8 GiB; MemAvailable +2.42 GiB | 381,513 -> 452,900 tokens (+18.7%) |
| median ITL c=1 / c=4 / c=8 | -4.0% / +6.9% / +8.8% | +1.4% / +3.0% / +6.8% |
| GSM8K-256, 5-shot (%) | 97.7 -> 98.0 | 96.9 -> 97.3 (mean of 2) |

The ITL cost is the per-call scale expansion; this is a capacity trade. Spark c=1 is within run-to-run noise (89.65 and 88.53 ms on two other nodes). ITL rather than TPOT because MTP acceptance varied (2.03 to 2.26).

The numbers were measured with the earlier in-tree encoder. FlashInfer's encoder produces byte-identical streams (checked on GB10 for Flash-Next expert shapes at TP1/2/4, up to 10.4M exceptions per layer), so they carry over. The RTX PRO 6000 arm ran on a6b2e2c, before the port to main; the B12X path is unchanged since.

## Test Plan

On DGX Spark, image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-153dc04646` (FlashInfer 0.7.4) with this branch's files overlaid:

```text
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_b12x.py    # 48 passed
pre-commit, incl. mypy                   # passed
```

`test_b12x_compressed_csf_scales_match_decoded_scales` (Flash-Next shapes, TP1/2/4) checks that every expert's expanded scales are byte-equal to the decoded ones, and that CUDA graph replays with the scratch poisoned between them match the decoded-scale kernel: bit-exact at one token (micro kernel), within 0.25 at 64 (the dynamic kernel sums experts with atomics).

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP4-Local --served-model-name flashnext \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --dtype bfloat16 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --moe-backend b12x \
  --language-model-only --no-enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 32768 \
  --max-num-seqs 8 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --compilation-config '{"max_cudagraph_capture_size":32}' \
  --kv-cache-memory-bytes 8G --gpu-memory-utilization 0.80 \
  --engram-config '{"disk_offload":true,"cpu_offload":false}'   # Spark
  # RTX PRO 6000: --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 instead of the last two lines
vllm bench serve --backend openai --model flashnext --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 --num-prompts $((8*C)) \
  --max-concurrency $C --ignore-eos --seed 0          # C = 1, 4, 8
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-questions 256 --temperature 0 \
  --max-tokens 512 --use-chat-completions --model flashnext \
  --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}'
```
</details>

AI assistance was used for code, tests and the measurement harness. I reviewed every line and ran the tests and benchmarks above. Not a duplicate: #65240 does the same for MXFP4 W4A8 scales (opt-in) and touches the same B12X plumbing; no open PR keeps NVFP4 `csf` scales compressed on the GPU.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Fix EAGLE-3 on Transformers backend VLMs
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fix EAGLE-3 with Transformers backend VLMs, reported in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/66581#issuecomment-6855979586.

## Claims

- EAGLE-3 works with VLMs on the Transformers backend (e.g. Qwen2.5-VL, Idefics3) instead of failing at startup with `assert isinstance(model_output, tuple)`.
- Re-enables the `qwen3_eagle3-transformers` EAGLE-3 correctness test on CUDA, which was skipped for memory since https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/30566 and now fits (one item of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/38379).
- Aux hidden states are recorded by forward hooks on the decoder layers instead of HF's `OutputRecorder`s, because composite models (e.g. `LlavaModel`) rebuild the decoder output and drop the recorded outputs. The full model forward is always called, with or without EAGLE-3.

## Validation

Repro: Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct + `vllm-project/qwen2.5-vl-7b-eagle3-sgl`, `num_speculative_tokens=3`, 2 text prompts + 1 image prompt, greedy, 1x B200.

<details>
<summary>repro.py</summary>

```python
import sys

from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
from vllm.assets.image import ImageAsset

model_impl = sys.argv[1]
llm = LLM(
    model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct",
    model_impl=model_impl,
    max_model_len=4096,
    disable_log_stats=False,
    max_num_seqs=8,
    gpu_memory_utilization=0.5,
    limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 1},
    speculative_config={
        "method": "eagle3",
        "model": "vllm-project/qwen2.5-vl-7b-eagle3-sgl",
        "num_speculative_tokens": 3,
    },
)
image = ImageAsset("stop_sign").pil_image
messages = [
    [{"role": "user", "content": "Write a short story about a lighthouse keeper."}],
    [{"role": "user", "content": "Explain how a binary search works."}],
    [
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": [
                {"type": "image_pil", "image_pil": image},
                {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this image in detail."},
            ],
        }
    ],
]
outputs = llm.chat(messages, SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=256))
for o in outputs:
    print(repr(o.outputs[0].text[:150]))
```

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][XPU] Use int64 token index in the DeepSeek-V4 qnorm/RoPE kernel
commits.pr_body:
- **Problem:** `_xpu_qnorm_rope_kernel` (`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/xpu/xpu_qnorm_rope_kv_fp8_insert.py`) computes `token_idx * num_heads * HEAD_DIM` in int32, so the Q address wraps once a step holds more than 2^31 Q elements (65,536 tokens with 64 local heads); on Intel Arc Pro B60 this ends in `UR_RESULT_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST`. The 1M-context DeepSeek-V4 models hit this with a single prompt over 65,536 tokens at TP=1 and `--no-enable-chunked-prefill`. Fixes vllm-project/vllm#52416.
- **Fix:** promote `token_idx` to int64 (as the sibling DeepSeek-V4 kernels `fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant.py` and `fused_mtp_input_rmsnorm.py` in `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/common/ops/` already do), which also widens the KV offset; `head_idx` stays int32 because `head_idx * HEAD_DIM` is at most 128 × 512. A new regression test calls the public `xpu_qnorm_rope_kv_fp8_insert` op past the boundary, and a new Intel kernels CI step runs it.
- **Validation:** on Intel Arc Pro B60 with `vllm/vllm-openai-xpu@sha256:14d76dee` (nightly, 2026-10-29) on `main` 5082c45853, `pytest tests/kernels/test_deepseek_v4_xpu_qnorm_rope_large_batch.py -v` gives 1 passed with this PR and 1 failed (`UR_RESULT_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST`) without it; below the boundary (4096×64, 8192×8, 8192×64, 32768×16 tokens × heads) Q and the KV cache are bitwise identical to `main` and the op time is within ±0.1%. The new test is short and cheap: a single case on one card, about 15 s for the whole pytest session including the vLLM import (15.5 s with this PR, 16.1 s on `main`), and it needs about 8 GiB of free device memory, skipping otherwise.
- **Not a duplicate:** this supersedes vllm-project/vllm#52427 (same cast, applied to both program ids, no test; closed by its author on 2026-09-20 without a maintainer review) and adds the regression test and CI step it lacked; no open PR references vllm-project/vllm#52416; vllm-project/vllm#46685 (merged) and vllm-project/vllm#52582 fix the overlapping-store bug in the same kernel and do not touch the index type.
- **AI assistance:** this PR was written with AI assistance; I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

commits.pr_title: [CI][ROCm] Bake torchao into the ROCm test image off the default path and re-enable MI300/MI355 Quantization
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

This PR changes the ROCm side only: it bakes torchao into the ROCm test image off the default path and re-enables the MI300 and MI355 DPX Quantization jobs that #63608 disabled.

**Stacked on #66194.** Until #66194 merges, this PR's diff also shows its commit, which bakes torchao and conch into the CUDA image and re-enables H200 Quantization. Those lines are reviewed in #66194. Review only the `[CI][ROCm]` commits here.

Trunk change: needs line-by-line review (step commands and the ROCm test image).

Why torchao can't sit in site-packages: transformers imports it at load and torchao queries the GPU at import, so tests that fork fail. On ROCm that showed up as `test_registry_inspect_does_not_init_cuda` failures and "fork needs to be used for the engine core process". Upstream: pytorch/ao#5086, huggingface/transformers#50540.

## Claims

- A `build_torchao` stage (`FROM dev`) installs `requirements/test/quantization_deps_rocm.txt` with `--require-hashes --no-deps --target /opt/quantization-deps`, and the per-commit `test` stage copies the folder in with `COPY --link`. The lock holds plain `torchao==0.18.0` from PyPI and is compiled from #66194's `quantization_deps.in` with `--no-deps` and conch left out (ROCm already ships conch in `requirements/rocm.txt`) by a new `pip-compile-quantization-deps-rocm` hook.
- The stage installs torchao's `py3-none-any` wheel, which has no compiled extensions, and fails if any `.so` lands in the folder. The other wheel only adds CUDA extensions that can't load on ROCm.
- The stage sits below the per-commit marker and the lock is not in the image cache key, so a torchao bump rebuilds only the `test` stage, not the runtime or test-deps images.
- `test-smoke` fails the build if torchao is findable on the default path, or not findable with `PYTHONPATH=/opt/quantization-deps`.
- Restored: the `:amd: (MI300) Quantization` mirror (`automatic_shard: true`) and the `test-amd.yaml` MI300 and MI355 DPX Quantization jobs, with no tests skipped or deselected. Each exports `PYTHONPATH=/opt/quantization-deps${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}` before its pytest commands and lists the torchao lock in its source dependencies.
- `tests/rocm/test_moe_padding.py` and `test_moe_weight_replay.py` leave the tethering allowlist.

## Validation

- `pre-commit run` on the changed files: all hooks pass, including both torchao lock hooks and the tethering check. `tests/tools/test_rocm_build.py`: 47 passed.
- Pipeline generator: nightly and run-all gain exactly `amd-quantization`. The planner parses its commands (1 setup line, 3 pytest commands) and plans 3 shards.
- On MI300X, with torchao from this lock placed off the default path the way CI does it, on main with #66875 and #66876:
  - `test_online_shared_expert_fusion.py`: 47 passed, 3 skipped (before #66875, its three `routed_mxfp8` cases failed).
  - `-k routed_mxfp8` and `test_online_lut_b_moe`: 10 of 10 repeated runs passed.
- On MI355X, `test_online_lut_b_moe` passes through the emulation backend with #66876, and `tests/kernels/moe/test_lut_b_moe.py` gives 8 passed and 7 skipped (native-GEMM-only cases).
- The `build_torchao` install was checked locally: `py3-none-any`, no `.so`, imports on ROCm torch.
- Not checked yet: the ROCm image build itself and the `test-amd.yaml` jobs, which render through the AMD pipeline. `/ci run` and a scoped build of the optional AMD Quantization jobs are pending.

## Details

- Separate stage, as the ROCm owners asked. Below the marker it costs one small layer per bump and otherwise hits the CI cache.
- The lock isn't added to `ci_config_rocm.yaml`'s run-all list, because other jobs can't see torchao. The Quantization steps' source dependencies cover a bump.
- MI300 moves from torchao 0.17.0 to 0.18.0, matching CUDA. One `.in` holds one version.
- The tests that failed on ROCm when the jobs came back are fixed on main, so this PR needs no test changes: #66875 (`routed_mxfp8` scale-layout check, #66861) and #66876 (`lut_b_moe` allowed on ROCm).
- **Planned simplification:** after vllm-project/ci-infra#825 merges (the shard plugin also goes into site-packages, so a command's own `PYTHONPATH` can't hide it), each `export` line becomes a plain `PYTHONPATH=/opt/quantization-deps` prefix on the pytest line, as in #66194.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm] Minimax M3.1 attn indexer XCD balancing
commits.pr_body:
## Overview
At 9-48 requests, decode attention put too much work on some XCDs resulting in imbalance and low GPU utilization. The indexer read and dequantized each index-K page twice for 8-row requests. The new plan balances the XCDs, and the indexer reads each page once.

## Claims
Improve performance on gfx942 and 950 by balancing requests across XCDs.


## Validation
µs per layer, 128K context: 
9-10 req 16.6-17.1→15.0-15.7; 
17-24 req 29.6-31.1→22.1-22.8; 
33-40 req 47.1-49.4→34.5-35.3; 
41-48 req 43.4-44.9→35.0-36.6.
Indexer push: 
12 req × 64K 14.2→12.2 µs; 
16 × 131K 23.4→17.1; 
24 × 250K 45.9→29.4.

A request is DSpark + 1 rows / tokens.

Eval | With our changes | Baseline (stock main)
-- | -- | --
GSM8K (flexible / strict) | 0.846 / 0.831 | 0.844 / 0.826
GPQA-Diamond | 84.09% | 82.68%

## Details
None beyond what is stated in the overview. This is simple GPU load balancing across WGs.

commits.pr_title: [Recipe] Kimi-K3.1-Pro: MI355X AgentX preset covering all six InferenceX#5043 concurrencies
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Replace the two Kimi-K3.1-Pro MI355X AgentX presets from #67487 (`mi355x_agentx` at concurrency 48 and `mi355x_agentx_c1` at concurrency 1) with one `mi355x_agentx` preset whose points cover every concurrency of the MI355X vLLM AgentX lane in [InferenceX #5043](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/5043) (`kimik3.1-fp4-mi355x-vllm-agentic-dspark`): 1, 4, 16, 24, 32 and 48.

## Claims

- One preset, "AgentX TP8", with six concurrency points that the builder can render:
  - **1:** plain TP8 (the preset's three DCP flags removed), GPU KV, low-latency decode, 7 DSpark draft tokens, `--max-num-seqs 1`, `VLLM_KIMI_SD_DSA_PROLOGUE=1`.
  - **4:** DCP8, GPU KV, low-latency decode, 5 draft tokens, `--max-num-seqs 2`.
  - **16 / 24 / 32:** DCP8 with Simple host KV offload, `--max-num-seqs` 8 / 13 / 20, 4 / 4 / 3 draft tokens, `--prefill-schedule-interval 32` with `VLLM_PREFILL_CADENCE_NO_ESCAPE=1`. Concurrency 32 also uses `--max-num-batched-tokens 10240` and 0.91 memory utilization.
  - **48 (default point):** DCP8 with host KV offload, 3 draft tokens, `--max-num-seqs 48`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 10240`, 0.91 memory utilization.
- Every point's generated command carries the same serving flags and environment variables as the InferenceX run for that point.
- `?preset=mi355x_agentx` still renders the concurrency-48 command #67487 published, unchanged apart from JSON key order. The concurrency-1 command moves from `mi355x_agentx_c1` to that preset's `c1` point, with the same argv and env.
- The image is pinned to the digest InferenceX measured (`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:kimi-k31-6d74a15@sha256:c470d0de…`), on the same tag as before.
- The runbook gives per-point interactivity and throughput, GSM8K, and the image-only switches.

## Validation

From a `vllm-project/recipes` checkout at `e5279d7`, with this branch as the `vllm` source:

```bash
node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm --dir "$VLLM_CHECKOUT/recipes"
node --test scripts/test-guide-html.mjs scripts/test-presets.mjs scripts/test-schema.mjs
pre-commit run typos --files recipes/models/moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro.yaml   # typos v1.51.1
```

- The source validator passes.
- 49 of 49 renderer tests pass.
- `typos` passes.
- Building the JSON API on `main` and on this branch gives 23,370 identical files. The only differences:
  - `moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro/presets/mi355x_agentx.json` changes.
  - `presets/mi355x_agentx_c1.json` is gone.

All six rendered commands were compared flag by flag with the `vllm serve` commands and environment in the InferenceX job logs. They match at every point, with these expected exceptions:
- The harness flags (`--host`, `--port`, `--device-ids`, `--served-model-name`) and harness environment variables (`VLLM_PORT`, `VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_*`) are not part of the preset.
- Throughput runs used synthetic acceptance where the preset keeps block rejection.
- Throughput runs also dropped the tool-call and reasoning parsers, which the preset keeps.

Existing GPU evidence, not a new GPU run from this PR: [InferenceX run 43399050596](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/43399050596) at `34099327` passed all six performance points (single run) and GSM8K at four concurrencies.

| Concurrency | Interactivity p50 / p90 (tokens/s/user) | Total tokens/s per GPU | GSM8K strict EM (1,319) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 239.0 / 231.4 | 2,033 | 0.979 |
| 4 | 180.7 / 164.0 | 3,076 | 0.981 |
| 16 | 102.4 / 81.7 | 8,901 | – |
| 24 | 81.4 / 66.0 | 13,198 | – |
| 32 | 66.2 / 56.6 | 15,331 | 0.980 |
| 48 | 38.7 / 23.4 | 19,201 | 0.981 |

## Details

**Not a duplicate.** This supersedes the concurrency-1 and concurrency-48 presets that #67487 added. Open PRs that touch this model are code changes, not recipe presets.

**Removed preset.** The `mi355x_agentx_c1` preset key and its `#preset-mi355x_agentx_c1` anchor no longer exist. Nothing else in `recipes/` or `vllm-project/recipes` links to them. The concurrency-1 point now applies its differences as point deltas:
- `remove_args` removes the three DCP flags.
- `select` turns low-latency decode on and KV offload off.

**Image-only switches.** The pinned image carries kernels and switches that vLLM main does not have yet. On main, these environment variables are not read:
- `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_DCP_VERIFY`
- `VLLM_ROCM_DCP_*`
- `VLLM_ROCM_DSA_*`
- `VLLM_ROCM_MEM_HEADROOM_GIB`
- `VLLM_KIMI_SD_DSA_PROLOGUE`
- `VLLM_PREFILL_CADENCE_NO_ESCAPE`

The low-latency decode backend on main also does not serve K3.1 without DCP, so the concurrency-1 point fails at startup on main or nightly images. The runbook says this. `--prefill-schedule-interval` is on main.

**Low-latency decode at concurrency 1 vs 4.** The server logs show different paths:
- **Concurrency 1:** the specialized decode runs the sparse MLA attention itself: the one-launch prologue, the indexer's scoring, and DSA split-K with 16 splits.
- **Concurrency 4, under DCP8:** the MLA and DSA layers run vLLM's attention ops, and the rest of each layer is fused.

**Throughput measurement.** The runbook's last section explains how to reproduce the AgentX throughput numbers:
- Synthetic acceptance at InferenceX's K3.1 DSpark golden acceptance length: 3.69 for 7 draft tokens, 3.41 for 5, 3.19 for 4 and 2.88 for 3.
- Parsers off, because the Kimi parsers stop streaming on unverified draft tokens.

It warns never to use synthetic acceptance for serving or accuracy.

AI assistance was used (Claude Opus 5.5, `claude-opus-5-5`, via Claude Code): it drafted the preset, ran the validation above, and compared the rendered commands with the InferenceX job logs. The submitter reviewed the changes.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Size the MOSS-Audio profiling dummy to its audio budget
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

MOSS-Audio's profiling dummy is a 1 s clip, while its per-item audio budget is a 30 s clip (`DEFAULT_MAX_AUDIO_SECONDS`), so startup profiles 13 audio tokens per item instead of 375. This makes the dummy a clip of the declared 30 s budget at the processor's mel sample rate. Split out of #67353 on review.

## Claims

- The MOSS-Audio audio dummy now has 375 embeddings, equal to the per-item audio budget (main: 13).
- Startup profiling now runs the encoder on 30 s dummy clips, so it may reserve more encoder memory and leave less for the KV cache; GPU memory was not measured for this change. It covers items up to the declared budget, not longer inputs.

## Validation

CPU (`VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`):

```text
$ pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_moss_audio.py
# main (new test only)
E       assert 13 == 375
1 failed, 15 warnings in 0.44s
# this PR
20 passed, 15 warnings in 4.14s
```

`test_common.py` skips MOSS-Audio by design ("Its vLLM processor paths are covered by test_moss_audio.py").

## Details

- **Root cause.** `MossAudioDummyInputsBuilder.get_dummy_mm_data` passed `length=16000` samples, one second, while `get_mm_max_tokens_per_item` declares a full `DEFAULT_MAX_AUDIO_SECONDS` clip.
- **Fix.** The dummy length is `mel_sr * DEFAULT_MAX_AUDIO_SECONDS`, with `mel_sr` read from the processor's mel config, so it follows the sample rate the processor uses.
- **Not a duplicate.** No open or closed PR changes the MOSS-Audio dummy (searched `moss_audio`, `MOSS-Audio`, `MossAudio`, `moss audio dummy`, `moss_audio.py in:files`; #46623, #51894 and #66820 touch audio paths but not this builder).
- **Related.** #67353 limits encoder co-scheduling to the tokens profiled at startup; with the 13-token dummy, MOSS-Audio would co-schedule fewer clips per step there, so this should land first. #67112 is the same fix for Gemma 4.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Return 400 instead of 500 when tool parsing is disabled
commits.pr_body:
## Overview The Rust frontend returns HTTP 500 for a chat request with `tools` when tool parsing is disabled, while the Python frontend returns 400. This PR adds `ParserDisabled` to `is_request_validation_error`, so the Rust frontend also returns 400. No other requests are affected: `ParserDisabled` is only raised in `resolve_tool_parser`, which only runs when tool parsing is enabled for the request. The gRPC `RenderChat` endpoint added in #65994 goes through the same `prepare` and maps errors with `is_request_validation_error` in `chat_error_to_status`, so it now returns `INVALID_ARGUMENT` instead of `INTERNAL` for this case as well; a gRPC test covers it. ## Validation **Reproducer (before the fix)**, `vllm/vllm-openai:latest` (v0.32.0), `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, no tool parser flags: ```bash curl -s -w '\nHTTP %{http_code}\n' localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What is the weather in Taipei?"}], "tools":[{"type":"function","function":{"name":"get_weather", "parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"city":{"type":"string"}}, "required":["city"]}}}]}' ``` | Frontend | Status | Message | |---|---|---| | Python | 400 | `"auto" tool choice requires --enable-auto-tool-choice and --tool-call-parser to be set` | | Rust | 500 | `failed to submit chat request: tool parsing is disabled by frontend configuration` | **Regression test**: `chat_completions_with_tools_returns_400_when_tool_parser_disabled` in `rust/src/server/src/routes/tests.rs` sends the request through the HTTP route against the mock engine, with the tool parser set to `ParserSelection::None`. - With the fix: passes (400, `BadRequestError`). - Without the fix (reverting `rust/src/chat/src/error.rs`): fails with `left: 500, right: 400`. **gRPC test**: `render_chat_rejects_tools_when_tool_parsing_is_disabled` in `rust/src/server/src/grpc/tests.rs` sends the same tools to `RenderChat` with tool parsing disabled. - With the fix: passes (`INVALID_ARGUMENT`). - Without the fix: fails with `Status { code: Internal, message: "tool parsing is disabled by frontend configuration" }`.
Details **Root cause.** The request path is `chat_completions` → `ChatLlm::chat` → `ChatRequestProcessor::prepare` → `DefaultChatOutputProcessor::with_response_template` → `resolve_tool_parser`. When the tool parser selection is `None`, `resolve_tool_parser` returns `vllm_chat::Error::ParserDisabled { kind: "tool" }`. The handler maps it with `chat_submit_error`, which returns 400 only when `is_request_validation_error()` is true. `ParserDisabled` was not in that list, so it fell through to `server_error!` (500). **Why 400.** The client can fix the request by removing `tools`, like other errors already in the list such as `UnsupportedMultimodalContent` (an image sent to a text-only model). `rust/AGENTS.md` also asks for parity with the Python frontend's error status codes. Returning 500 makes clients treat a healthy server as faulty: OpenAI SDKs retry 5xx, and it counts toward server-error alerting. **Not a duplicate.** #62321 and its work (`/tokenize` by @MuonChaser, `/detokenize` in #62775) cover endpoints that wrap every error in `server_error!`. Here, `/v1/chat/completions` already uses `chat_submit_error`; the gap is a single missing variant in `is_request_validation_error`. I found no open issue or PR for this case (searched for `tool parsing is disabled`, `is_request_validation_error`, and Rust frontend tool parser / status code PRs). **Deviation from Python.** The status code now matches, but the message does not: Python names the flags to set, while Rust only says tool parsing is disabled. Aligning the message is out of scope for this PR. **Testing scope.** Error mapping is validated with the in-process HTTP route test and the gRPC render test, following the Validation section of `rust/AGENTS.md`. The tests assert the status code and error type only; I can also assert the message if preferred. **Follow-up.** `ParserUnavailableForModel` (parser selection `Auto`, but no parser is known for the served model) also returns 500. I left it out because it looks closer to a server configuration problem that is better detected at startup; #64069 adds a startup warning for it.
**AI assistance.** AI assistance (Claude) was used to analyze the code path and draft this PR. I reviewed every changed line, traced the root cause, ran the tests above, and verified the reproducer myself. ---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Audio] Fall back to soundfile when torchcodec fails to decode
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Since #58364 made torchcodec the first `auto` audio backend, any torchcodec decode error is final. MP3s with an occasional undecodable frame, which decoded fine when soundfile came first, now return `400 Invalid or corrupted audio data`. This PR lets `auto` retry such inputs with soundfile before rejecting them.

## Claims

- `load_audio(backend="auto")` decodes MP3s that FFmpeg aborts on but libsndfile reads, restoring the behaviour from before #58364 for these files.
- When soundfile can't read the input either, the original torchcodec error is raised and PyAV is still skipped, so an FFmpeg decode that has already failed is never repeated.
- Duration and memory-limit rejections are unchanged and never fall back.

## Validation

Reproducer: long-form MP3s that contain an undecodable frame (`[mp3float] Header missing`) about every 330 s, probably the seams of concatenated segments. The `ffmpeg` CLI skips these frames and exits 0, but PyAV and torchcodec abort on the first one. Two such files (38 and 43 min, 44.1 kHz stereo, 128 kb/s) decode with each backend as follows (FFmpeg 6, torchcodec 0.17, PyAV 19.0.2, libsndfile 1.2.2):

| Backend | File 1 | File 2 | Control MP3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| soundfile | OK | OK | OK |
| torchcodec | FAIL | FAIL | OK |
| PyAV | FAIL | FAIL | OK |
| `auto` on `main` | FAIL | FAIL | OK |
| `auto` with this PR | OK | OK | OK |

File 1 is `fireside_chat_w_mistral_ceo_arthur_mensch.mp3` and File 2 is `state_of_gpt_BRK216HFS.mp3`, both from the public [amgadhasan/longform-audio-transcription](https://huggingface.co/datasets/amgadhasan/longform-audio-transcription/tree/main/audio) dataset. To reproduce (torchcodec must be able to load its FFmpeg libraries; otherwise `auto` on `main` falls back to soundfile and the file decodes):

```bash
curl -sLO https://huggingface.co/datasets/amgadhasan/longform-audio-transcription/resolve/main/audio/state_of_gpt_BRK216HFS.mp3

python3 - <<'EOF'
from vllm.multimodal.media.audio import load_audio

f = "state_of_gpt_BRK216HFS.mp3"
for backend in ["soundfile", "torchcodec", "pyav", "auto"]:
    try:
        audio, sr = load_audio(f, sr=16000, backend=backend)
        print(f"{backend:10} OK   {len(audio) / sr:.0f}s")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"{backend:10} FAIL {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
EOF
```

On `main`:

```text
soundfile  OK   2560s
torchcodec FAIL ValueError: Invalid or corrupted audio data. Ensure the input is a valid audio or video file (e.g. a complete WAV, MP3, or MP4).
pyav       FAIL ValueError: Invalid or corrupted audio data. Ensure the input is a valid audio or video file (e.g. a complete WAV, MP3, or MP4).
auto       FAIL ValueError: Invalid or corrupted audio data. Ensure the input is a valid audio or video file (e.g. a complete WAV, MP3, or MP4).
```

With this PR, the last line becomes `auto       OK   2560s`.

End to end, I served `CohereLabs/cohere-transcribe-03-2026` on an H100 with a full FFmpeg install, so torchcodec works, and set `VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_CLIP_FILESIZE_MB=50 VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_DECODE_DURATION_S=3600`. Each MP3 was posted to `/v1/audio/transcriptions`:

| | File 1 | Control MP3 |
|---|---|---|
| `main` | `400 Invalid or corrupted audio data` | 200 |
| This PR | 200, correct transcript | 200 |

The same failure also broke a downstream concurrent long-audio streaming CI test; it passes with this change (WER unchanged).

Tests: `pytest tests/multimodal/media/test_audio.py` gives 24 passed. The 4 torchcodec tests fail identically on `main` on my dev host, because its system FFmpeg is incomplete (`Could not load libtorchcodec`). They don't involve this change. `pre-commit` passes.

No new test is added: a regression test needs an MP3 with a corrupted frame. I can add one if reviewers want it.

## Details

**Root cause.** #58364 moved torchcodec ahead of soundfile in `auto` and kept the rule that a decode error doesn't fall through, because FFmpeg-based PyAV would fail the same way. That rule is right for PyAV, but soundfile now sits between them and doesn't use FFmpeg: its MP3 decoder (mpg123) resyncs past bad frames that FFmpeg's decoder rejects with `avcodec_send_packet: Invalid data found`.

**Change.**
- torchcodec open and decode failures now raise `_CorruptAudioError`. It is a private `ValueError` subclass with the same message, so the API still returns 400.
- In `auto`, that error falls through to soundfile only.
- If soundfile then fails (an unrecognised format, a corrupt file, or soundfile not installed), the torchcodec error is re-raised and PyAV is skipped.
- The duration and memory-limit `ValueError`s are not `_CorruptAudioError`, so they still raise immediately.

**Tradeoff.** For input that is truly corrupt, `auto` now also pays for a soundfile attempt after the failed torchcodec decode. soundfile enforces the same duration and memory limits, so that cost is bounded.

**Not a duplicate.** I searched open PRs and issues for torchcodec / soundfile / fallback / `load_audio`. #54334 is about torchcodec *import* errors in the video decoder, and #51894 adds an audio channel-count limit; neither changes the `auto` fallback order. Companion PR: #67106, caching torchcodec's library-load failure and honouring `audio_backend` in the speech-to-text endpoints (separate change, same file).

AI assistance (Claude) was used for the root-cause analysis, the implementation and the validation runs.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] SIGTERM only the managed engine's launcher so in-flight requests drain
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On shutdown, `vllm-rs serve` sends SIGTERM to the managed engine's whole process group. The GPU worker processes exit on SIGTERM, so in-flight requests fail a few seconds after the signal instead of draining for `--shutdown-timeout`. This PR sends SIGTERM to the Python launcher only, which already drains and then stops the engine cores and workers in order. It keeps the process-group SIGKILL as the timeout fallback.

## Claims

- On SIGTERM, `vllm-rs serve` drains in-flight requests for up to `--shutdown-timeout`, as `vllm serve --headless` does, instead of killing them when the workers exit.
- A launcher that does not exit in time is still SIGKILLed with its whole process group, and the group is SIGKILLed once more after the launcher exits, to catch stragglers.
- With the API server, `vllm-rs serve` now drains the API server first while the engine keeps serving, and stops the engine afterwards with the remaining budget, as `vllm serve` does.

## Validation

Unit tests in `vllm-managed-engine`, with a shell-script launcher whose process tree stands in for the engine:
- `shutdown_signals_only_launcher_and_reaps_process_group`: the launcher gets SIGTERM, its child does not, and the child is gone after shutdown. With the previous group SIGTERM restored, this test fails (`assertion failed: !dir.path().join("grandchild-term").exists()`: the child received SIGTERM).
- `shutdown_kills_group_when_launcher_ignores_sigterm`: a launcher that ignores SIGTERM is SIGKILLed with its group after the timeout.

```
cd rust
cargo clippy --all-targets -p vllm-managed-engine -p vllm-cmd -- -D warnings
cargo nextest run -p vllm-managed-engine -p vllm-cmd
```

`cargo fmt --check`, clippy: clean. nextest: 129 passed, 0 failed.

Before the fix, on a Kubernetes pod running `vllm-rs serve` with two local data-parallel engines and `--shutdown-timeout 360`, we deleted the pod with 11 long streaming requests in flight:
- Both engine cores started draining ("draining in-flight requests count=5" and "count=6").
- About 6 s after SIGTERM, the GPU worker processes of both engines exited ("Worker proc ... died unexpectedly").
- All 11 requests ended mid-stream with "engine core reported fatal failure".

End to end on one GB200 with Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B (dense), `vllm-rs serve --data-parallel-size 2 --shutdown-timeout 120`: two streaming chat completions pinned to each rank with `X-data-parallel-rank` (`ignore_eos`), 300 tokens each on rank 0 and 4000 tokens each on rank 1, then SIGTERM to `vllm-rs` once every stream has produced tokens. Times are seconds after SIGTERM; `vllm-rs` exits with status 0 in every run.

| Build | Rank 0 streams | Rank 1 streams | `vllm-rs` exit |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | error at 2.3 (`engine core reported fatal failure`) | error at 2.3 (same) | 9.0 |
| main + launcher-only SIGTERM (`170342b1cb`) | complete (`length`) at 6.3 | error at 9.5 after ~470 tokens (`engine core EngineId(0000) disconnected`) | 81.9 |
| this PR | complete at 6.0 | complete at 80.4 | 85.5 |

With launcher-only SIGTERM alone, rank 0 finishes its drain and exits, and its disconnect fails the requests still running on rank 1, while rank 1 keeps generating them until it exits. With the API server drained first, both ranks serve every stream to completion, and the engine is stopped afterwards with the remaining 39.5 s, exiting 5 s later.

Still to do before this leaves draft: rerun that reproducer with the fix, then compare against the `vllm serve --headless` drain.

## Details

**Root cause.** `ManagedEngineHandle` starts the Python launcher in its own process group (`setpgid(0, 0)`) and, on shutdown, signalled `-pgid`. That group includes every process the launcher starts:
- The launcher itself (`run_headless` in `vllm/entrypoints/cli/serve.py`) handles SIGTERM by raising `SystemExit`. It then calls `engine_manager.shutdown(timeout=shutdown_timeout)`, and the engine cores drain their requests before stopping their executors.
- The multiproc executor's workers (`WorkerProc` in `vllm/v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py`) also turn SIGTERM into `SystemExit`. So the group SIGTERM stopped the workers underneath the engine cores that were still draining.

With `vllm serve --headless` under a process manager, only the launcher receives the signal, which is why that path drains correctly.

**Fix.** `shutdown` now SIGTERMs the launcher's pid alone. The two existing safety nets stay:
- SIGKILL to the whole group if the launcher has not exited within `max(timeout, MIN_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT)`.
- One more group SIGKILL after it exits, to reap anything left behind. An already-empty group (`ESRCH`) counts as success.

**Tradeoff.** A launcher that exits without stopping its children now relies on that final group SIGKILL instead of the first SIGTERM. Apart from the shutdown order below, nothing outside `ManagedEngineHandle::shutdown` changes, and there is no new flag.

**Shutdown order.** `vllm-rs serve` used to SIGTERM the engine as soon as shutdown began, so the engines drained alongside the API server. Data parallel ranks of a non-MoE model drain independently and exit one by one, and since vllm-project/vllm#67187 the client fails every request once any engine disconnects, so the first rank to finish would cut the drain of the others short (MoE ranks keep stepping until the whole group is idle and exit together). `main.rs` now waits for the API server to drain before stopping the engine with the remaining budget, which matches `run_multi_api_server` in `vllm/entrypoints/cli/serve.py`. With `--headless` the engine still gets the whole budget and drains under the launcher.

No existing PR or issue covers this. I searched open and closed PRs and issues for managed-engine shutdown, process-group SIGTERM and the Rust frontend drain.

commits.pr_title: [Spec Decode][MRV2] Build no draft attention metadata on a context-K/V-only prefill
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Follow-up to #65217. With `prefill_context_kv_only`, the DFlash-family drafter on a P/D prefill instance only writes its context K/V and never runs draft attention, yet the target model runner and the drafter both create metadata builders for the draft layers. A FlashInfer draft builder allocates a prefill workspace sized for the full batch (`max_num_batched_tokens` × query heads × head_dim × 16 B) after the memory profile, and the target runner builds draft metadata every step. This PR keeps the draft attention groups and their kernel-block layout but creates no builders for them.

## Claims

- On a context-K/V-only prefill instance, the draft layers get no metadata builders:
  - no FlashInfer workspace for the draft: two fewer with a FlashAttention target, one fewer with a FlashInfer target (whose own workspace stays);
  - no draft metadata built per step, and the draft backend no longer limits the target's CUDA graph mode.
- The memory goes back to the KV cache. With the extensible KV cache (the CUDA default), the workspaces took KV cache blocks; where the KV cache is sized from the memory profile (e.g. `kv_cache_memory_bytes`, or NIXL without an IMEX channel), they came on top of `--gpu-memory-utilization`.
- Unchanged: the draft's kernel block size and cache layout (which the decode instance reads), KV cache binding and zeroing, the decode instance, and everything without `prefill_context_kv_only`.

## Validation

1P1D on one GB300 node over NixlConnector, `main` (`df5d80339b`) and this PR side by side, both prefill instances with `prefill_context_kv_only`:
- `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` + `z-lab/Qwen3-8B-DFlash-b16` (k=16), draft on FlashInfer, `--max-num-batched-tokens 32768`: each draft workspace is 32,768 tokens × 32 query heads × 128 × 16 B = 2 GiB.
- 24 greedy chat requests one at a time, then 8 concurrent ~6.7K-token prompts, so prefill steps reach the token cap.

| Target backend | Draft workspaces on prefill (`main` → PR) | Prefill KV cache blocks after warmup | Decode outputs | Decode drafts / accepted, one-at-a-time requests |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FLASH_ATTN | 2 × 2 GiB → 0 | 20,720 → 21,120 (+1.9%) | 32/32 identical | 1,381 / 3,385 in both |
| FLASHINFER | 1 × 2 GiB → 0 | 20,680 → 20,880 (+1.0%) | 32/32 identical | 1,349 / 3,353 in both |

Peak allocated memory through the 32,768-token prefill steps dropped by the same 4 GiB and 2 GiB (25.46 → 21.46 GiB and 25.85 → 23.84 GiB), CUDA graph capture took 2.57 GiB in both stacks, and the decode instances are identical. Over the concurrent burst, drafts differ by at most one between stacks, and `main` alone gave 67 or 68 from run to run; an A/A run of two `main` stacks matched exactly. In one of two runs of the FlashAttention arm, one of the 8 concurrent long prompts diverged near the end of its 32 tokens (31/32 identical); the repeat and the A/A were 32/32.

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py tests/v1/worker/test_kv_block_zeroer.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_warmup_blocks.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_lookahead.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_context_kv_modules.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_target_dependent_ar_speculator.py \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_recoverssm_state.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_draft_attention_backend_override.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_eagle_draft_attn_metadata.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_hybrid_model_state.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_varlen_cudagraph.py
```

On one GB300 GPU this PR passes all 277 tests; with `main`'s `vllm/`, 276 pass and the new test fails:

```
FAILED tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py::test_no_attn_metadata_layers_keep_their_layout_without_builders
E       TypeError: init_attn_backend() got an unexpected keyword argument 'no_attn_metadata_layer_names'
```

The new test runs `init_attn_backend` with a target backend and a draft backend whose builder owns a workspace, in one 256-token KV cache group where the draft takes kernel blocks of up to 64 tokens. With the draft layer in `no_attn_metadata_layer_names`, nothing is allocated, the CUDA graph support is the target's, the varlen CUDA graph check passes, the kernel block size stays 64, and `build_attn_metadata` returns only the target's metadata. Without `groups_with_metadata_builders` in `get_attn_cg_support`, `get_varlen_cudagraph_unsupported_backend` or `build_attn_metadata`, it fails on `get_metadata_builder`'s assert.

I also ran on GB300 the CI steps that this PR's files select, each with its commands from `.buildkite/test_areas` on the GPU count it asks for. That is the 24 per-PR steps whose dependencies name a changed file, plus the nightly spec-decode steps that cover them, 27 after merging duplicates:
- per-PR: spec decode, V1 core/worker/KV connectors/KV offload/metrics, CUDA graphs, ReplaySSM, fault tolerance, distributed, Kimi K3;
- nightly: DFlash, DFlash2, DSpark and MTP acceptance rates, Eagle, speculators and draft-model e2e, speculator correctness, GSM8K with DSpark on DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Kimi K3 prefix cache.

16 pass. In the other 11, each failing test either also fails with `main`'s `vllm/` or passes when rerun alone. The causes are unrelated to this change and mostly specific to this machine: gated checkpoints, NIXL-EP and Mooncake setup, FlashInfer TRT-LLM kernels missing for this GPU, `os.memfd_create` missing from this Python build, NUMA-bound worker spawns. The steps that select this PR only through `vllm/` are left to CI, as are the kernel steps selected by the one-line stand-in fix in `tests/kernels/attention/`, a file the GPU unit-test run above includes.

## Details

On `main`, on a prefill instance with `prefill_context_kv_only` and a FlashInfer draft:

1. `determine_available_memory` profiles the model and sets the KV cache budget; no attention backend exists yet.
2. `initialize_kv_cache` calls `init_attn_backend` over every KV cache group, the draft's included. The draft builder allocates its workspace, or shares a FlashInfer target's.
3. `DraftModelSpeculator.set_attn` calls `init_attn_backend` for the draft layers, and its builder allocates a second workspace.
4. Every step, the target runner builds the draft groups' metadata; the drafter only stores its context K/V.
5. The decode instance reads the target and draft K/V over the KV connector.

With this PR, steps 2 to 4 create and build nothing for the draft layers.

`AttentionGroup.create_metadata_builders` sets up the kernel-block layout and creates the builders. The drafter still needs the layout: it computes its context K/V slots from the group's kernel block size and stride, the KV cache is bound and zeroed through the groups, and a KV cache group's kernel block size is chosen over all its groups' backends, which fixes the layout the decode instance reads. So the groups stay and only the builders go:

- `init_attn_backend(..., no_attn_metadata_layer_names=...)` asks `create_metadata_builders` for zero builders for groups made only of those layers, so their `metadata_builders` is empty and their kernel-block layout is set up as before. Their kernel block table, one row per builder, has no rows: only metadata builds and the drafter's full-CUDA-graph draft step read it, and a context-K/V-only drafter never drafts.
- The target runner and `DraftModelSpeculator.set_attn` pass the draft layers when `prefill_context_kv_only` is set.
- Code that reads builders skips groups without them through one helper, `groups_with_metadata_builders`: `get_attn_cg_support`, `get_varlen_cudagraph_unsupported_backend`, `build_attn_metadata`, `DraftModelSpeculator._configure_decode_metadata_update`, DFlash's `aot_schedule` loop, and the RecoverSSM paths that walk all of the runner's groups (`RecoverSSMState.record_step`, Kimi K3's `DeferredRecoverSSMState.bind`). The drafter's draft step, which updates metadata in place, needs no change, since a context-K/V-only drafter never drafts, nor do DeepSeek-V4.1's specialized-decode metadata graphs, which refuse KV transfer.
- Stand-in groups in five existing test files now also set `metadata_builders`, and the stand-in drafter in `test_drafter_uses_the_kernel_block_size_the_cache_was_allocated_with` sets `speculative_config`.

Related: #65089 (opt-in FlashInfer workspace sizing at startup, which excludes spec decode).
