commits.pr_title: [ROCm] Keep the extensible KV cache for fd-exporting KV connectors
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On ROCm, `_resolve_extensible_kv_cache` rejects every connector whose `kv_cache_access` needs a single physical chunk, including `EXPORTS_FD`. The stated reason (UCX/RDMA cannot register driver-mapped memory) only applies to `REGISTERS`. This narrows the ROCm check to `REGISTERS`, so connectors that import the KV cache in another process through POSIX fds (e.g. `LMCacheMPConnector` in VMM mode) keep the extensible KV cache on ROCm instead of failing at startup.

Related: LMCache/LMCache#6626 adds the ROCm side of LMCache's VMM KV-cache import.

## Claims

- On ROCm, a connector declaring `KVCacheAccess.EXPORTS_FD` no longer makes `VllmConfig` raise `enable_extensible_kv_cache: ... on ROCm, UCX and RDMA cannot yet register driver-mapped memory`; the extensible KV cache stays on by default and an explicit `--enable-extensible-kv-cache` is accepted.
- `REGISTERS` connectors (NIXL, Mooncake, MoRIIO, UMBP) on ROCm behave as before: extensible KV cache off by default, explicit request is an error.
- CUDA is unaffected.

## Validation

Unit test (new `test_extensible_kv_cache_on_for_rocm_fd_exporting_connector`), fails without the fix with the `ValueError` above and passes with it; the existing ROCm `REGISTERS` test still passes:

```bash
pytest tests/v1/engine/test_engine_args.py -k "extensible_kv_cache_on_for_rocm_fd_exporting or extensible_kv_cache_off_for_rocm_registering or nixl_needs_an_imex"
```

| Source | Result |
|:--|:--|
| `main` (`d64414d04`) | 2 failed (new test), 7 passed |
| this PR | 9 passed |

Full `tests/v1/engine/test_engine_args.py` in a GPU-less container: the same 11 tests fail on `main` and on this PR (`RuntimeError: Failed to infer device type`); the only difference is the new test (fails on `main`, passes here). `pre-commit run --files vllm/config/vllm.py tests/v1/engine/test_engine_args.py` passes.

End to end on 8x MI355X (gfx950), `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100` (`0.34.0rc1.dev398+g153dc0464`) with this one-line change applied, LMCache `dev` + LMCache/LMCache#6608 + LMCache/LMCache#6626, LMCache's ROCm 10 MP stress script (`Qwen/Qwen3-14B`, TP=8, `LMCacheMPConnector` with its default config, which declares `EXPORTS_FD`):

| Run | Result |
|:--|:--|
| Without this change | vLLM exits during `VllmConfig` construction with the `ValueError` above |
| With this change, 50 repeated 4096-token prompts per pass, 2 min | extensible KV cache on (`191424 KV cache blocks (233.67 GiB) fit within the requested 244.79 GiB`), 8 ranks x 40 KV cache fds exported to the LMCache server, 12 passes, 4400/4400 KV retrieves, 0 errors |
| With this change, 2000 x 4096-token prompts per pass, 10 min | 5 passes, 80412 KV stores, engine alive, 0 errors |

## Details

`needs_single_chunk()` is true for `REGISTERS | EXPORTS_FD | EXPORTS_FABRIC`. It is the right predicate for the single-chunk allocation itself (`registers_kv_cache_memory`, unchanged here), but the ROCm limitation behind this branch, per its TODO, is UCX's handling of `HSA_EXT_POINTER_TYPE_HSA_VMEM` and `hsa_amd_portable_export_dmabuf` on VMM ranges, which only matters when the KV cache is registered for RDMA. An fd-exporting connector exports each chunk with `hipMemExportToShareableHandle` and the other process maps it with `hipMemImportFromShareableHandle`: exercised end to end above on HIP 7.16, and checked standalone (export, import, map, read back) with torch `2.11.0+rocm7.2` on HIP 7.2.

`EXPORTS_FABRIC` on ROCm still falls through to the existing IMEX-channel handling; no ROCm connector declares it.

No open PR or issue covers this (searched open PRs for `needs_single_chunk`, `EXPORTS_FD ROCm`, `KVCacheAccess ROCm`, `extensible kv cache ROCm`).

commits.pr_title: [BugFix] Fix Mistral3 multimodal offline example
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix #33828: the Mistral3 offline vision-language example fails with one image and zero image placeholders. Use the native Mistral tokenizer and `llm.chat()` to insert the required image tokens.

## Claims

- Restore single-request and batched image generation for `mistral3`.
- Preserve processed images when `--image-repeat-prob` is set, and explicitly reject unsupported `--verify-mm-cache-hit-with-uuids`.
- Load Mistral-format weights while ignoring `model*.safetensors` to avoid duplicate downloads.

## Validation

Rebased the six original commits onto `cbe948fe0c7f3db65b9f5bc9ec50754c706d0cd9`; tested the exact clean checkout `e566709e84ac512ee45f53fb81a8cfb9d0ad67c2` on NVIDIA GB300 with TP=2. Model: `mistralai/Mistral-Small-3.1-24B-Instruct-2503`. Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, transformers 5.22.2, mistral-common 1.13.1; isolated editable vLLM installation with precompiled native extensions.

The base example was run in the same environment and reproduced:

```text
RuntimeError: Expected there to be 1 prompt placeholders corresponding to 1 image items, but instead found 0 prompt placeholders!
```

Run the following command from the checkout, adding the options in the table:

```bash
.venv/bin/python examples/generate/multimodal/vision_language_offline.py \
  --model-type mistral3 --modality image --tensor-parallel-size 2
```

| Case | Additional options | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Single | `--num-prompts 1` | PASS: 1 nonempty output |
| Batch | `--num-prompts 4 --use-different-prompt-per-request` | PASS: 4 nonempty outputs |
| Repeat probability 0 | `--num-prompts 4 --use-different-prompt-per-request --image-repeat-prob 0` | PASS: 4 nonempty outputs |
| Repeat probability 1 | `--num-prompts 4 --use-different-prompt-per-request --image-repeat-prob 1` | PASS: 4 nonempty outputs |
| Processor cache disabled | `--num-prompts 1 --disable-mm-processor-cache` | PASS: 1 nonempty output |
| UUID verification guard | `--num-prompts 1 --verify-mm-cache-hit-with-uuids` | PASS: expected ValueError stating this option is unsupported |

Generated descriptions mention cherry blossoms and a tower, consistent with the input image on visual inspection. This is an end-to-end functional smoke test, not a model accuracy benchmark or cache-hit measurement. Full Buildkite coverage remains subject to repository CI.

`ruff-check`, `ruff-format`, `typos`, SPDX headers, boolean-context-manager, forbidden-imports, and torch.cuda-call pre-commit checks passed for the changed file. `git diff --check` passed. Full local logs, environment metadata, exact commands, and generated outputs were archived.

## Details

The hand-written `[IMG]` text is not sufficient to insert native Mistral image tokens. The Pixtral processor expects those tokens to have been inserted during chat encoding. The example now follows the existing Mistral chat pattern with native tokenizer/config/load formats. The change is confined to the example harness; other models keep their existing path.

This addresses the example's input construction, separately from the processor compatibility work in #41948. The current baseline reproducer confirms that the example still needs this fix. Prior review feedback about image-repeat processing, UUID verification, weight filtering, and output formatting is incorporated.

commits.pr_title: [CI][ROCm][Kimi-K3] Compile each TP8 mono build and line the ranks up before launching it
commits.pr_body:
File: `tests/models/kimi_k3/amd_specialized_decode/test_numerics.py`.

### Purpose

`test_m1_tp8_dcp8_matches_vllm_ops_and_replays` in `kimi-k3-specialized-decode-amd` (8x MI355X) flakes. **No tolerance is involved.** The failures are gross or bit-exact mismatches:

| build (date) | where | assertion |
|---|---|---|
| 99504, 99719 ×2, 99839, 99929, 99934, 99977, 100096, 100321 (Nov 2–5) | first S=16 launch | M1: `AssertionError: 16` (health/flags, or padded query ≠ pad) or `32`; same job: `test_k2_tp8_opt_bits_are_bit_exact` `(16, False, 3, 0)` and mostly `test_k2_tp8_matches_vllm_ops_and_replays` |
| 100771 (Nov 7) | M1a S=32 | `q` rel-L2 **0.82** (bound 3e-2) with health and flags clean |
| 101820 (Nov 11, main) | M1a S=4, padded launch | `runner.health` set (a wait gave up) |

The test failed in 11 of ~490 jobs that ran it. The Nov 2–5 pattern (~6% of runs) stopped after the AITER v0.1.28.post1 bump (#65937, 2026-11-06). The residual rate is ~0.4%. Other failures in the step, such as a 25-min HF Hub hang in `test_m1a_pad_through_aiter_cprr[4]` (101034) and PR-specific breakages (100950, 101444), are unrelated.

### Root-cause hypothesis

Every M1/K2 TP8 worker in this file launches each FlyDSL build the first time on the spot. Each rank then JIT-compiles it on the host for several seconds, while the ranks that finished compiling are already running the kernel and spinning on its mailbox words. The in-kernel cross-rank waits give up after `WAIT_SECONDS` (10 s). A rank that gives up finishes the step on stale words and still tags its outputs. Its peers then read wrong values with **clean** health, which explains 100771 and the padded-query mismatches. The rank that gave up reports `health` set, which explains 101820 and the `AssertionError: S` cases.

What the logs show:

- Failing tests die early. The M1 test dies at 44–95 s against ~212–392 s when it passes, and the K2-opt test at ~57 s against ~120–210 s. That is during the first launches of new builds, which is where compile time dominates. A passing M1 run spends roughly 7–12 s of host time per new build key, about the same as `WAIT_SECONDS`.
- Phase 1 always broke at the first S=16 build, the first "large" key in both tests' S order. Phase 2 broke at random S.
- The engine never compiles between cross-rank launches: `runtime/decode.py` calls `compile_build` on every build at warm-up. So production does not have this skew.

Not reproduced, because no GPU was available. A real cross-rank race in the M1a DCP query gather (QG) would also explain the wrong-data cases. If failures continue after this change, add `given_up_waits(runner.health.cpu(), mla.REGIONS)` and a per-source-rank `q` error to the M1a asserts to tell the two apart.

### Change (test only)

- `_launch_together(key)`: if the build key is new, `compile_build(key)` (the engine's warm-up function), then `dist.barrier` on the TP CPU group. It is called before every `mla_pre`, `mla_post` and `k2_launch` in the TP8 workers, and skipped during graph capture.
- `_together()` before the first `graph.replay()` of each captured graph, whose capture may have compiled new keys.
- No tolerance, kernel or production-code change.

### Duplicate check

`gh pr list -R vllm-project/vllm --state all --search` for "test_m1_tp8_dcp8", "Kimi-K3 M1a", "kimi k3 specialized decode flaky" and "Kimi-K3 mono race" found nothing related. The local branch `vllm-fix-kimi-k3-adaptive-stub` targets a different test (`test_amd_kda_checkpoint.py`).

### Test plan / results

- `pre-commit run --files tests/models/kimi_k3/amd_specialized_decode/test_numerics.py`: all hooks pass.
- Not run on GPU. Needs `pytest -v -s tests/models/kimi_k3/amd_specialized_decode/test_numerics.py -k "tp8 or stalled"` on 8x MI355X, ideally `test_m1_tp8_dcp8_matches_vllm_ops_and_replays` in a loop (≥50 runs) with and without the change, plus a check that the test's wall time does not grow (compile time only moves earlier).

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to analyze the CI history and write this change. It has not been run on a GPU yet.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Stub dcp_world_size in the merged-cache sparse MLA test
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Stub `dcp_world_size` on the hand-built impl in `test_sparse_mla_backend_forward_mqa_fp8_ds_mla_merged_cache`. The gfx950 attention-kernels shard fails with `AttributeError` after #65685. Same pattern as #66798.

## Claims

- `forward_mqa` no longer raises `AttributeError: 'ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl' object has no attribute 'dcp_world_size'` on this test.
- World size 1 skips the DCP branch, so `dcp_rank` and `dcp_scores` are not read.

## Validation

Failing job: [amd-ci #15822, MI355 Attention Kernels Shard 1](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15822/list?jid=01a1d45d-0562-448f-816e-1061c8a8504b&tab=output), main @ `191e5d5d`. The test is `@requires_gfx950`, so the MI300 mirror skips it.

Local repro on MI300X (gfx942), image `rocm/vllm-ci:build-01a1d459-8a8f-4ee8-a118-ccbc91bb8a1e`, GPU 0, test function called directly:

- Unfixed: `AttributeError` at `rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py:1480`, matching CI.
- Fixed: that error is gone. The call reaches `aiter` `sparse_mla_fwd`, which rejects fp8_ds_mla on gfx942 (native fp8 is fnuz). The numeric check was not run here. MI355 is the hardware that executes this kernel.

## Details

The test builds `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl` with `object.__new__`, which skips `AttentionImpl.__new__`, the only place that sets `dcp_world_size`. #65685 added `if self.dcp_world_size > 1` at the top of `forward_mqa`. #66798 already had to stub `owns_indexer` and `index_epoch` on this same object four days earlier.

`dcp_world_size = 1` matches a non-DCP run and leaves the rest of the test on the path it was written for.

commits.pr_title: [Perf] Optimize Garbage Collection at Init Time
commits.pr_body:
## Overview
Better optimizes garbage collection for at init time to speed up manually `gc.collect()`s in the KV cache allocation.

## Claims
Currently, there are a lot of direct `gc.collect` calls when initializing vLLM, which add up over time. We can improve the startup time by temporarily freezing gc before loading the model, then unfreezing, collecting, and refreezing later on. This is useful for excluding things like imports references from the heap scans.

This currently gives a mostly flat speedup in initialization time of 3-4 seconds per model at the moment on both the cold and hot paths.

## Validation
Example startup bench with a small model: ` vllm bench startup --model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --num-iters-warm 5` on this branch vs main; you should see about 3-4 seconds difference for both the cold and hot case. Example below, compile metrics omitted since they don’t change really.

On main:
```
COLD STARTUP:
Avg startup time: 60.36 seconds
Startup time percentiles:
  10%: 58.51 seconds
  25%: 58.95 seconds
  50%: 59.68 seconds
  75%: 61.43 seconds
  90%: 62.48 seconds
  99%: 63.11 seconds

WARM STARTUP:
Avg startup time: 25.28 seconds
Startup time percentiles:
  10%: 24.81 seconds
  25%: 24.98 seconds
  50%: 25.25 seconds
  75%: 25.61 seconds
  90%: 25.78 seconds
  99%: 25.88 seconds
```

Vs this branch 
```text
COLD STARTUP:
Avg startup time: 54.12 seconds
Startup time percentiles:
  10%: 53.85 seconds
  25%: 53.93 seconds
  50%: 54.06 seconds
  75%: 54.28 seconds
  90%: 54.42 seconds
  99%: 54.50 seconds

WARM STARTUP:
Avg startup time: 22.86 seconds
Startup time percentiles:
  10%: 21.47 seconds
  25%: 21.58 seconds
  50%: 21.61 seconds
  75%: 21.92 seconds
  90%: 25.44 seconds
  99%: 27.55 seconds
```

You can also validate this directly by adding timing hooks around garbage collection. 
```python
import gc
import os
import time

os.environ["VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING"] = "0"

from vllm import LLM

MODEL = "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B"

# Timing and counts per generation
gc_secs = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
gc_counts = [0, 0, 0]
t0 = 0.0


def on_gc(phase: str, info: dict[str, int]) -> None:
    """Start / stop callbacks for garbage collection to help measure time diffs."""
    global t0
    if phase == "start":
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        return
    gen = info["generation"]
    gc_secs[gen] += time.perf_counter() - t0
    gc_counts[gen] += 1

if __name__ == "__main__":
    gc.callbacks.append(on_gc)
    start = time.perf_counter()
    LLM(MODEL)
    startup = time.perf_counter() - start
    gc.callbacks.remove(on_gc)
    print(
        f"startup {startup:.2f}s  GC {sum(gc_secs):.2f}s  "
        f"gen0/1/2 secs {gc_secs[0]:.2f}/{gc_secs[1]:.2f}/{gc_secs[2]:.2f}  "
        f"counts {gc_counts[0]}/{gc_counts[1]}/{gc_counts[2]}"
    )
```

Running this on this branch on main can let you more easily check that the savings are from the gc collects.
```
Main: startup 27.62s  GC 9.18s  gen0/1/2 secs 0.13/0.11/8.94  counts 2333/212/23
This branch: startup 23.44s  GC 5.57s  gen0/1/2 secs 0.12/0.10/5.35  counts 2332/209/25
```

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Disagg][CI] Give Wide-EP headless nodes the KV config
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Wide-EP headless nodes are started without `--kv-transfer-config`, so no KV connector is created on them.

- MoRIIO: ranks 8–15 never open their handshake and notify ports. After [vllm-project/router#386](https://github.com/vllm-project/router/pull/386) the router schedules all 16 DP ranks per role, so KV for ranks 8–15 does not transfer.
- NIXL: the connector is never created on the headless nodes, and 2P2D hangs until the 1800 s gloo timeout.

## Changes

`.buildkite/amd-disagg/vllm_disagg.sh`, `build_ep_cmd`:

- Pass MoRIIO `--kv-transfer-config` on the headless child and the master.
- `remote_hosts`: the other role's node IPs, master first.
- `remote_dp_size_local`: `GPUS_PER_NODE`. Rank `r` dials `remote_hosts[r / GPUS_PER_NODE]` at port offset `r % GPUS_PER_NODE`.
- NIXL headless nodes get the NIXL config that the master gets.
- `fill_remote_pod_from_config` copies those two fields onto the request when the router omits them. The decode rank holding the request sends the notify.
- The WRITE release for a request aborted before it is scheduled fills them too, so it reaches the pod that owns the peer rank.

commits.pr_title: [CI][Multimodal] Use `uuid:`-tagged cache key for features in /generate test and docs
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix `test_features_with_content_parts[True]`, which has failed on every `main` build since #66473 merged, along with the matching `/inference/v1/generate` docs example. Both still referenced a cached multimodal item by its bare `uuid` (`"old"` / `"img-a"`). Since #66473, the processor cache key of an item sent with a `uuid` is `uuid:<uuid>`.

Failing job: `:amd: (MI355 DPX) Entrypoints Integration (API Server) Shard 2`. First failing build: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/102595 (#66473). It has failed on every build since, e.g. https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/102603. Last pass: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/102593.

## Claims

- `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_serving_multimodal_tokens.py::test_features_with_content_parts[True]` passes again.
- The docs example in `docs/serving/online_serving/token_in_token_out.md` now uses the cache key the server actually uses (`uuid:img-a`) and says how that key is formed.
- No change under `vllm/`.

## Validation

GPU: AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950), 1 GPU. Image: `docker.io/rocm/vllm-ci:build-01a1d693-b016-423a-b642-1381b3802ebf`, the CI image from failing build #102603. Tests run from `/vllm-workspace/tests`.

Before (unmodified test from the image), reproducing the CI failure:

```
$ pytest -v -s entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_serving_multimodal_tokens.py -k test_features_with_content_parts
(EngineCore) WARNING [core.py:2355] Multi-modal cache miss for request generate-tokens-8052f4a2ceab5660-9373d9d5 (mm_hashes=['old']): P0/P1 cache drift; returning a retryable response so the items are resent with data.
INFO:     127.0.0.1:46930 - "POST /inference/v1/generate HTTP/1.1" 500 Internal Server Error
FAILED entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_serving_multimodal_tokens.py::test_features_with_content_parts[True]
====== 1 failed, 1 passed, 4 deselected, 16 warnings in 70.79s (0:01:10) =======
```

After (this PR's test file mounted into the same image):

```
$ pytest -v -s entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_serving_multimodal_tokens.py
...::test_render_to_generate_roundtrip PASSED
...::test_content_parts_generates_tokens PASSED
...::test_features_with_content_parts[False] PASSED
...::test_features_with_content_parts[True] PASSED
...::test_content_parts_before_features_is_rejected PASSED
...::test_content_parts_streaming PASSED
======================= 6 passed, 16 warnings in 58.12s ========================
```

CPU: `pre-commit run --files` on both changed files passes (ruff, mypy, markdownlint, typos, docstring style).

## Details

Root cause: a semantic merge race between two PRs.

- #57796 (merged 2026-11-12) added `features` + `content_parts` support to `/inference/v1/generate`. Its docs and test resend an item cached by turn 1 with `features.mm_hashes = {"image": ["<uuid>"]}` and no `kwargs_data`, relying on the bare `uuid` being the processor cache key.
- #66473 (merged 2026-11-13, CI run before #57796 landed) domain-separates cache keys: `ProcessorInputs.get_mm_hashes` now returns `content:<digest>` for content hashes and `uuid:<uuid>` for caller uuids.

So turn 1 caches the item under `uuid:old`, and turn 2 asks for `old`. The engine reports a P0/P1 cache miss and the request fails with a 500. The failure doesn't depend on the platform. It is in the frontend's cache-key logic, and the same tests run in the H200 API Server step.

I kept this to the test and docs rather than having the server map untagged `features.mm_hashes` to `uuid:`. Hashes taken from a render response are already tagged, and a caller `uuid` may itself start with `content:`. A server-side mapping would therefore have to guess which domain a key belongs to, which undoes the separation #66473 introduced. If maintainers prefer a compatibility path for clients that send bare uuids, that can follow separately.

Duplicate check: no open or merged PR touches `test_serving_multimodal_tokens.py` or this docs example since #66473. #67400 (Rust frontend parity) and #67461 / #67561 (other mm hash fixes) do not change it.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to triage the failure and prepare this change. The GPU validation above was run on MI355X with the CI image.

commits.pr_title: [Feature][EPD] Support Kimi-K3 image metadata-only inputs
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Support metadata-only image inputs for Kimi-K3 and Kimi-K3.1 in EPD. Related: #52409.

## Claims

- Publish only original image dimensions through the existing EC metadata contract; consumers derive embedding token counts from their vision configuration.
- Reconstruct identical image placeholders on consumers without preprocessing the images again.
- Accept precomputed image embeddings in the NVIDIA and AMD model implementations.

## Validation

Real Kimi-K3 encoder weights on GB200 produced finite embeddings matching the consumer-computed token counts. This was rerun after the review revision with EC metadata containing only `image_sizes`. Feeding that metadata to the consumer frontend reproduced the raw-image prompt exactly: 1,045 tokens, with image embedding counts `[204, 512, 1, 204]`. Repeated UUID metadata and precomputed-embedding splitting also passed.

### Review revision validation

- CPU processing suite: **7 passed**, including metadata-only chat rendering and roundtrips with and without precomputed embeddings. Token IDs, placeholder ranges, and per-image embedding slices match the raw-image path.
- GB200 smoke through `LLM.generate` with real encoder weights: passed. Published metadata contains only `image_sizes`; consumer-computed placeholder lengths match actual encoder outputs, repeated UUIDs share an EC entry, and precomputed-embedding splitting passes.
- All pre-commit hooks, including mypy: passed.
- Reproduced the failure from [Buildkite #101666](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/101666#01a1c8e6-d6df-42f8-a033-fcb2b9e2a42b) on `b1496cc17695`: `--mamba-block-size can only be set with --enable-prefix-caching`. The frontend test now disables prefix caching before hybrid-cache defaults are derived, keeping the configuration consistent with CPU MLA. The test still exercises real chat rendering.
- The dimensions-only regression test fails on `b1496cc17695` because EC metadata also contains `image_num_tokens`; it passes after moving count calculation to the consumer.

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu \
    .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
    tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_kimi_k3.py -v
# 7 passed
```

### Consumer frontend benchmark (original implementation)

These measurements precede consumer-side token-count recomputation and have not been rerun for this revision.

Kimi-K3, same commit (`a7483f54f3`), 16 pinned Grace CPU cores, 8 Torch/Numba threads, one renderer worker, and a 4 GiB LRU processor cache. Two runs per arm in A/B then B/A order, each in a fresh frontend process; preparation, initialization, and disjoint synthetic warmup are excluded.

- **Miss:** 512 MUIRBench requests / 2,232 images, with unique UUIDs and verified 0% processor-cache hits.
- **Hit:** 32 hot requests repeated to 512 requests, with verified 100% processor-cache hits on the raw-image path. Metadata-only bypasses this cache.

Here, cache means the **consumer frontend multimodal processor cache** (`mm_processor_cache_gb`), not encoder embedding cache or KV/prefix cache.

| Processor cache | Concurrency | Mean frontend latency, ms (raw → metadata) | Frontend req/s (raw → metadata) | Throughput change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Miss | 1 | 72.7 → 25.8 | 13.73 → 38.66 | +181.6% |
| Miss | 32 | 1820.8 → 836.7 | 17.13 → 37.27 | +117.6% |
| Miss | 96 | 5222.3 → 2408.0 | 17.06 → 36.85 | +116.0% |
| Hit | 1 | 39.9 → 25.7 | 25.06 → 38.92 | +55.3% |
| Hit | 32 | 892.4 → 813.8 | 34.71 → 38.09 | +9.7% |
| Hit | 96 | 2514.8 → 2306.9 | 34.85 → 37.85 | +8.6% |

CPU time per request fell by approximately **90% on misses** and **69% on hits**. All 12,288 rendered outputs matched the raw-reference token IDs and placeholder ranges; paired-run throughput differences were at most 2.1%.

These are frontend-only measurements of `render_chat_async`, excluding HTTP transport, EC transfer, encoding, and LM execution. Higher-concurrency latency includes frontend queueing; the results do not establish end-to-end speedups.

<details>
<summary>Regression checks</summary>

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_kimi_k3.py \
    -k 'metadata_only or fused_image_processor' -v
# 5 passed
```

The new metadata roundtrip test fails on base `25a6a8bd10` with `KeyError: 'image_sizes'` and passes with this change.

</details>

Full proxy-to-GPU-consumer generation and Kimi-K3.1 hardware validation remain pending.

## Details

Kimi's image prompt includes the original width and height, not just the resized patch grid. Carry these dimensions and derive the embedding length on the consumer with `navit_resize_image` and the same vision configuration. `image_num_tokens` remains an internal field for embedding splitting and is not part of the EC metadata contract. Producer and consumer must use matching vision configurations. No proxy, scheduler, or connector changes are needed.

No duplicate open PR was found; #66849 adds video input, not this image metadata-only path.

AI assistance was used to develop this change.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Repeat-last default padding for `cu_seqlens` in multimodal CG
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #64984. When an encoder CUDA graph replay has fewer sequences than the capture, the manager's default copy zero-fills the end of `cu_seqlens`. A zero after the real total offset makes the padded sequences negative-length. FlashAttn and the other non-FlashInfer ViT backends then produce wrong encoder output for the real items.

This PR:

- Changes the manager default for cumulative keys (`cu_seqlens`, `cu_window_seqlens`) so it repeats the last value (suggested by @Pb314314). Other buffers are still zero-filled.
- Moves the FlashInfer `cu_seqlens` padding helper to `MMEncoderAttention.get_cu_seqlens_padding_logics`, next to `maybe_recompute_cu_seqlens`, which builds that layout. It uses the same OOT dispatch as `maybe_recompute_cu_seqlens`, so an OOT attention that changes the layout can also override the padding.

## Claims

- Models fixed by the new default:
  - GLM-4.1V/4.5V and the models that inherit its config (GLM-OCR, GLM-5.3-Flash).
  - Qwen2-VL, when `encoder_cudagraph_max_vision_items_per_batch` is set.
  - In both cases, video-enabled capture pads `cu_seqlens` to `max_frames_per_batch`, while image replays pad only to `max_batch_size`.
- FlashInfer backend: the packed two-section layout still needs its own padding. These models now get it from `MMEncoderAttention.get_cu_seqlens_padding_logics`:
  - Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL, which previously registered `_pad_flashinfer_cu_seqlens_buffer` themselves.
  - GLM-4.1V. With video enabled, image replays used a smaller batch bucket than the capture.
  - Kimi-K2.5. Capture pads to `max_batch_size + 1` but replays are unpadded, so the buckets differ once `max_batch_size >= 8`.
- Refactoring: per-model registrations that are now identical to the default are removed:
  - Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen3-VL and LFM2-VL: `_pad_cumulative_seqlens_buffer`.
  - Kimi-K2.5, DeepSeek-V4.1 and MiniMax-M3: `pad_cu_seqlens`.
- Pixtral, Cohere Compass and MiniMax-M3 also call `get_cu_seqlens_padding_logics`, so every encoder-CG model whose `cu_seqlens` comes from `maybe_recompute_cu_seqlens` takes its padding from one place. Without an OOT override, their padding is unchanged. See Details.

## Validation

```shell
pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py -v

# 101 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped in 41.67s
```

`TestFlashInferCuSeqlensPadding` replays `cu_seqlens` into a larger capture buffer through `MMEncoderAttention.get_cu_seqlens_padding_logics` and the manager's lookup, for FlashInfer and FlashAttn. With the old zero-fill default, the FlashAttn cases fail. A second test checks that an OOT `MMEncoderAttention` overrides the padding.

GPU validation of the GLM-4.1V FLASH_ATTN path by @Pb314314 ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65453#issuecomment-6645668754)): GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking on GB200, bf16, `limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 4, "video": 1}`. The table shows the relative L2 error of the graph output vs eager, one image per call.

| Image | Tokens | main | This PR | Eager in a 2-image batch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 224x224 | 64 | 0.20% | 0.20% | 0.20% |
| 336x336 | 144 | 106.8% | 2.70% | 2.70% |
| 448x448 | 256 | 169.1% | 2.36% | 2.36% |
| 672x672 | 576 | 169.4% | 0.18% | 0.19% |

GPU validation by `replay == eager` benchmark with dummy weight load (adapted from `test_eonly_vit_cudagraph_outputs` test script)

| model | FLASHINFER | FLASH_ATTN |
| --- | --- | --- |
| glm4_1v | pass | pass |
| qwen3_vl | pass | pass |
| kimi_k25 | pass | pass |
| minimax_m3 | N/A | pass |
| pixtral | *eager not runnable | *eager not runnable |

Note: My script cannot run pixtral ViT with eager mode, haven't fully understood why but at least I have checked that this is not a regression from this PR (pixtral Vit with eager fails on main as well).

## Details

- Removed registrations are equivalent to the new default:
  - Kimi-K2.5 and DeepSeek-V4.1 truncated with `min(src, dst)` when `src` was longer than `dst`. That branch never runs: each image is one sequence, so a replay has at most `max_batch_size + 1` offsets, and both models capture `max_batch_size + 2`.
- Newly wired models keep their in-tree padding:
  - MiniMax-M3 rejects FlashInfer, so it gets `{}` and the default, as before.
  - Pixtral and Cohere Compass (image-only) capture and replay `cu_seqlens` at the same length. Under FlashInfer, the helper then reduces to a plain copy.
- Not wired: DeepSeek-V4.1, Kimi-K3 and Qwen2-VL build their own `cu_seqlens` instead of calling `maybe_recompute_cu_seqlens`. They rely on the manager default.
- OOT: vllm-ascend overrides `EncoderCudaGraphManager._run_budget_graph` with its own copy of the old lookup, so the new default doesn't apply there. Its FIA path drops non-increasing `cu_seqlens` endpoints, so zero-fill and repeat-last give the same result.
- Not a duplicate: no other open PR changes this padding. #66067 (@Pb314314) is a pure refactor of the grid_thw encoder CG code and does not touch `cu_seqlens` padding.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write this PR body. I wrote every changed line with care and ran the unit tests above.

commits.pr_title: [CI][Bugfix] Fix fake backend in drafter kernel block size test
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`test_drafter_uses_the_kernel_block_size_the_cache_was_allocated_with` (`tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py`) has failed on `main` since #62800 landed. This PR adds the missing per-layer method to the test's fake attention backend. It is a one-line, test-only change.

Failing job: `:amd: (MI355 DPX) V1 Executor + Worker`. It failed on every attempt in builds [#102655](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/102655) (e9281bd, #62800) and [#102661](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/102661) (d64414d). The last passing build was [#102645](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/102645) (1ea7a90, #64777).

```
v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py:1318: in test_drafter_uses_the_kernel_block_size_the_cache_was_allocated_with
vllm/v1/worker/gpu/attn_utils.py:274: in init_attn_backend
vllm/v1/worker/utils.py:718: in prepare_kernel_block_sizes
vllm/v1/worker/utils.py:560: in select_common_block_size
E   AttributeError: 'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'get_supported_kernel_block_sizes_for_layers'
```

## Claims

- Fixes the `AttributeError` above, so `test_attn_utils.py` passes on `main` again.
- No production code changes.

## Validation

GPU validation used one MI355X (gfx950) inside the failing build's CI image, `docker.io/rocm/vllm-ci:build-01a1d758-0515-4882-9cb0-83b605623701`. The command ran from `/vllm-workspace/tests`:

```bash
pytest -v -rs v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py
```

Before the fix (stock image), the CI failure reproduces:

```
E           AttributeError: 'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'get_supported_kernel_block_sizes_for_layers'
FAILED v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py::test_drafter_uses_the_kernel_block_size_the_cache_was_allocated_with
============ 1 failed, 67 passed, 1 skipped, 16 warnings in 39.58s =============
```

After the fix (patched `test_attn_utils.py` mounted into the image), the whole file passes:

```
v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py::test_drafter_uses_the_kernel_block_size_the_cache_was_allocated_with PASSED [100%]
SKIPPED [1] v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py:586: HiSparse CUDA ops not compiled
================= 68 passed, 1 skipped, 16 warnings in 40.33s ==================
```

The skipped test is unrelated and was also skipped before the fix. `pre-commit run --files tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py` passes.

## Details

Root cause: #64777 and #62800 were merged close together and conflict with each other.

- #64777 added this test. Its fake backend is a `SimpleNamespace` that only defines `get_supported_kernel_block_sizes`.
- #62800 changed `select_common_block_size` to call `backend.get_supported_kernel_block_sizes_for_layers(spec, layer_names)` whenever layer names are passed. `prepare_kernel_block_sizes` always passes them.

#62800 added the per-layer method to the other fake backends in this file, but this test wasn't on `main` yet when #62800 was written. Real backends are unaffected because they inherit the method from `AttentionBackend`, which falls back to `get_supported_kernel_block_sizes`. This PR gives the fake backend the same per-layer method.

The test still checks what it was written to check. With per-layer lookup, the target (`[128]`) and draft (`[128, 512]`) layers in one 512-token group still resolve to 128, and the drafter is still built with 128.

Not a duplicate: no open or merged PR adds this method to this test's fake backend. #67291 and #67173 also edit `test_attn_utils.py`, but neither touches this backend. No commit after d64414d on `main` touches the file.

This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code) as part of AMD CI triage, and the human submitter reviews it.

commits.pr_title: [Recipe] Kimi-K3.1-Pro: MI355X kimi-k31-6d74a15 image, concurrency-48 with 3 draft tokens, align with InferenceX#5043
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Aligns the Kimi-K3.1-Pro recipe's MI355X presets with [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#5043](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/5043). That PR moves the K3.1 MI355X vLLM AgentX lane to the `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:kimi-k31-6d74a15` image (`sha256:c470d0de…`), returns the concurrency-48 point to 3 draft tokens without `--prefill-schedule-interval`, and adds new ROCm DCP/DSA env vars.

**Stacked on #66774** (InferenceX#4948, `kimi-k31-d73dd529`). That PR is still open, so this branch carries its commits. Only the last commit (`055ad9b1b8`) is new here; review that one, or merge #66774 first.

## Claims

- **AMD image → `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:kimi-k31-6d74a15`.** It reports the same vLLM version string (`0.0.0+mum.14d1ec2336`) as `kimi-k31-d73dd529` but carries newer ROCm K3.1 kernels and the env switches below. The image key, the guide text and the concurrency-1 runbook's digest now name this image.
- **`mi355x_agentx` (concurrency 48) follows InferenceX#5043's concurrency-48 point:**
  - The DSpark draft goes from 6 back to 3 tokens, still with block rejection.
  - The decode capture sizes return to 4–192 (step 4), which is 48 requests × (1 + 3). The prefill ladder now starts at 224 and still runs to 10240.
  - `--prefill-schedule-interval 8`, `--long-prefill-token-threshold 10240` and `--long-prefill-token-threshold-adaptive` are removed.
  - New env:
    - `VLLM_ROCM_DCP_VUP_RS=1`: the DCP combine applies `v_up` first, then AITER LSE all-gather plus reduce-scatter.
    - `VLLM_ROCM_DSA_MULTISTREAM=1`: in decode, the DSA indexer, the DCP score gather/merge and the gate run on an aux stream.
    - `VLLM_ROCM_MEM_HEADROOM_GIB=8`: keeps 8 GiB free for DCP prefill transients the memory profile misses.

    The server log of the CI run shows all three active.
  - The synthetic-acceptance snippet uses the golden acceptance length for 3 draft tokens, 2.88.
  - The `--max-num-batched-tokens` note now quotes the image's KV block size from the server log (`kv lcm block sizes 8192` under DCP8) instead of the old 1152-token packed DSA block.
- **`mi355x_agentx_c1` (concurrency 1)** keeps its args. Env changes:

## Overview

Grouped top-k routers (DeepSeek-V3/V3.2, GLM-4.5+/5, Kimi-K2/K3, MiMo-V2, ...) now give DP and CUDA-graph padding rows expert id -1 by default, as fused top-k routers already do, so modular MoE kernels skip them. Until now they did so only for models that opt in under DeepEP v2 (from #56079). Follows #65972, which did the same for the TRT-LLM block-FP8 / MXFP8 monolithic kernels.

## Claims

- **Higher DP + EP serving throughput, both runs better at nearly every concurrency, on three grouped top-k models and two MoE backends:**
  - GLM-5.3-NVFP4, DP8: +5% to +21% (concurrency 8 to 256);
  - MiMo-V2.6-Flash (MXFP4 experts), DP4: +5% to +7% at 16 / 64 / 256, +2.6% (within noise) at 4;
  - DeepSeek-V3.2-NVFP4, DP4: +3% to +8% at 4 / 16 / 64, +1.5% (within noise) at 256.
- **Accuracy unchanged:** GSM8K at concurrency 4 (every decode step mostly padding) and 256 on all three models, inside launch-to-launch variation.
- **One slower bucket:** DeepSeek-V3.2 at concurrency 256, decode steps with 33-128 rows per rank are 5.6% slower in both runs (13% of step time); throughput there is within noise.
- **No new option.** `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=0` turns masking off for all routers, as before.

**Serving.** Each model: Baseline = main 80e0cd68f8; After = the same tree with grouped top-k padding masking forced on through a local env switch at router construction. **Unit tests** (GB200):

```

  tests/kernels/moe/test_routing_simulator.py tests/kernels/moe/test_topk_softplus_sqrt.py
```

2800 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed. Also `tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer.py -k "routed or grouped"` (the #65972 routed path, whose runner no longer re-masks for grouped routers), `test_routed_experts_capture_monolithic.py` and `test_naive_dp_ep_dbo.py`: 81 passed.

- `test_grouped_topk_masks_padding[skip_env × skip_padding × use_fused]` (was `test_kimi_grouped_topk_masks_padding_when_enabled`): padded rows get -1 / weight 0 whenever `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING` is on, with or without the model flag, fused and unfused; with the env off nothing is masked; real rows are unchanged. On main, the four cases without the model flag fail.
- `test_grouped_topk_skips_mask_for_rows_gathered_before_routing[use_fused]`: with more router rows than mask rows, routing completes and masks nothing. It sets the model flag so main reaches the mask: on main both cases fail (the CUDA kernel's size check, or a shape mismatch in `masked_fill`), and they fail again on this branch with the length check removed.

## Details

**Why padding was not masked.** `GroupedTopKRouter` passes the runner's `is_padding` to its kernel only when `skip_padding` is set, and `FusedMoEFactory` sets it only for models that pass `skip_padding=True` (Kimi-K3) *and* use DeepEP v2 (`layer.py`). Every other grouped top-k model routes padded rows like real tokens, and modular kernels compute them.

**Changes.**
- `GroupedTopKRouter.masks_padding` is `skip_padding or not rocm_aiter_ops.is_fused_moe_enabled()`, matching `FusedTopKRouter` / `FusedTopKBiasRouter`. The mask itself is the one the router already applied under the opt-in: the CUDA kernel's `is_padding`, or `masked_fill` on the other paths. On ROCm AITER the opt-in still applies, since I did not check that AITER experts accept -1.
- `get_moe_padding_mask` returns `None` when the router sees more rows than the local mask covers. This happens when the runner all-gathers rows from every DP rank before routing (`MoERunner._maybe_dispatch`, for quant methods without an internal modular kernel). The local mask does not describe those rows, and the `topk_softmax` and `grouped_topk` CUDA kernels both check `is_padding.size(0) == num_tokens`, so passing it would raise. Those rows are routed without a mask, as before. This also applies to fused top-k routers.
- Docstrings of `skip_padding` and the `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING` comment updated.

**Affected models.** Every model whose MoE layers are built with `use_grouped_topk=True` and a non-degenerate grouping (`create_fused_moe_router` sends one-group, top-1-group routing that the fused top-k routers can express to them, and they already mask; e.g. LFM2-MoE without expert bias), when it runs a modular MoE kernel on CUDA, XPU or ROCm without AITER fused MoE and the step has padded rows (DP > 1, or CUDA-graph padding):
- DeepSeek-V2/V3/R1 and V3.2 (`DeepseekV2MoE`), and models built on them: Kimi-K2/K2.5, Kimi-VL, Mistral Large 3, A.X-K1, Unlimited-OCR, GLM-4.7-Flash (`glm4_moe_lite`), GLM-5 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`), plus their MTP/EAGLE drafters;
- GLM-4.5/4.6/4.7 (`glm4_moe`, MTP) and GLM-5.3 (`glm5next`);
- MiMo-V2 Flash/Omni (`mimo_v2`, MTP);
- Hunyuan (`hy_v3` with MTP, `hy_v4`), EXAONE-MoE (MTP), AFMoE, LFM2-MoE, OpenPangu (MTP), Nemotron-H MoE and the models built on it (Nano-Nemotron-VL, Cosmos3-Edge, Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe);
- when the checkpoint config sets `n_group`/`topk_group`: Bailing/Ling (`bailing_moe`, `bailing_moe_linear`), Sarvam, Param2MoE, Beam, and the Transformers-backend MoE;
- Kimi-K3: already masked under DeepEP v2 through its opt-in; now also on other all2all backends.

Not affected: DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 (own routing), LongCat-Flash (zero-expert router), models with plain softmax/sigmoid top-k (already masked by the fused top-k routers), CPU (`create_fused_moe_router` returns `CPURouter` there), ROCm AITER, and monolithic kernels that route from logits.

**Correctness on these models.** Masking changes only padded rows, whose outputs are discarded; the unit tests check that real rows get the same experts and weights. End to end I checked GLM-5.3-NVFP4, MiMo-V2.6-Flash and DeepSeek-V3.2-NVFP4 (GSM8K above); the other listed models rely on the argument below, not on their own runs.

**Why -1 is safe on the newly masked paths.** The expert backend is chosen by the quantization method, not the router, and fused top-k routers (e.g. Qwen3-MoE, MiniMax) already pass -1 for padded rows to the same modular experts and all2all backends by default; the EPLB mapping kernel maps -1 to -1 (`eplb_triton.py`); every grouped top-k implementation already supports `is_padding`.

**Unchanged.** Monolithic kernels that route from logits (they do not call the router; the #65972 path under DP already masked in the runner, and now the router does it instead), ROCm AITER, `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=0`.

**Limitations.**
- With sequence-parallel MoE (EP + TP > 1 + DP > 1, e.g. `deepseek_v2.py`), each TP rank routes its own chunk, but `is_padding` stays the full-batch mask, so `[:num_tokens]` gives every TP rank the first chunk's mask. Padding is always at the end of the batch, so this can only leave padded rows unmasked on TP ranks > 0, never mask a real token; fused top-k routers have the same limitation on main. Re-sharding the mask there is left for a follow-up.
- Kimi-K3 was not measured: its verified GB200 layouts are TP8 x PP2 (no DP padding) or DEP with DeepGEMM MegaMoE, which reads `is_padding` itself.
- Only ShareGPT; DeepEP LL/HT not measured.

**Not a duplicate.** I searched open PRs for grouped top-k / padding / `skip_padding` / `is_padding`. #50759 (draft, last updated 2026-09-02) applies a generic `torch.where` mask after every router in `BaseRouter`; its fused top-k and dsv4 parts have since landed on main through other PRs. It does not exclude ROCm AITER or guard rows gathered before routing. This PR only turns on the mask grouped top-k already implements and adds that guard.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this change and run the experiments. I reviewed every changed line and the measurements.

commits.pr_title: [KV Connector][NIXL] Pull KV from pipeline-parallel prefill stages, with the hybrid KV cache manager
commits.pr_body:
# Pull KV from pipeline-parallel prefill stages

## Overview

Enable pull KV transfer from a pipeline-parallel prefill instance (P) to a
PP1 decoder (D), including attention-only hybrid KV cache groups (HMA).
Addresses the prefill-side PP case in #52913, using the layer-aware region
pairing from #63416. PP stages hold different layers and may hold no layers of
some cache groups; D must select the owning stage for each transfer.

## Details

### Unified remote-stage state

Adopts @njhill's [remote-stage refactor](https://github.com/njhill/vllm/commit/548cb98227cd7932ce94a07359d6bf4fadb4a01f):

- All remote engines use `_remote_stages[engine_id][pp_rank]`; PP1 is one
  stage at rank 0. Each `_RemoteStage` owns region pairs, covered layers,
  selected-region capacities/group IDs and descriptor handles by TP rank.
- Handshake uses one registration path for PP1 and PP>1. Region capacities
  follow the selected descriptor order. TP ranks within a stage must agree on
  pairing, and the union of P stages must cover every required D KV layer
  exactly once.
- Pull iterates stages without separate PP1 state lookups. `_read_blocks`
  receives the resolved pairs, capacities, handle and notification agent.
  Push uses the same representation through `_single_remote_stage`, since D
  remains PP1. Engine cleanup releases the handles across all stages.

### Request flow and lifecycle

1. D handshakes with the required `(pp_rank, tp_rank)` workers and prepares
   layer/group mappings for their regions.
2. `_read_blocks_for_req` iterates TP `ReadSpec`s and remote stages. READs
   use that stage's mapping and handle; their number depends on TP mapping
   and the groups with blocks to read.
3. HMA is determined from the transfer cache-group specs, rather than only
   the layers held by the worker. Stages with no relevant blocks, including
   full prefix hits, are notified without posting a READ.
4. Each P worker reports local send completion after its expected consumer
   notifications. `KVOutputAggregator` combines completion from all P TP×PP
   workers before the P scheduler frees the request's blocks. A notify-only
   stage does not independently free them.

On a READ error, D stops posting sibling READs and drains outstanding handles;
destination blocks stay reserved until draining completes. Missing P
notifications use the existing send-lease expiry path and the same completion
barrier. D stops renewing leases on terminal receive completion or abort.
`recompute` means local D computation, not retrying READs against old P metadata.
The existing lease/drain failure model is unchanged; no transport cancellation
protocol is added.

### Pull configuration boundaries

`NixlConnector` defaults to pull mode (`NixlPullConnector`). The following
checks supplement existing model, TP, block-size and handshake compatibility
requirements:

| Configuration | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| P PP>1 → D PP1; dense or attention-only HMA; supported non-packed layouts | Accepted, with compatible per-layer cache-group assignments |
| D PP>1 with `kv_consumer` or `kv_both` | Rejected at connector construction, for pull and push |
| PP producer with `bidirectional_kv_xfer=true` | Rejected at connector construction, for pull and push |
| PP pull with `BLHNC` / `BHLNC` on either endpoint | Rejected locally at PP initialization or when the PP peer is identified at handshake, independently of the HMA flag |
| PP pull with HMA-required MLA / CSA-linear caches | Rejected; other MLA/CSA PP combinations are not validated here |
| PP pull with Mamba/SSM, DCP on either endpoint, or mixed-memory KV caches | Rejected at initialization or handshake |
| PP pull with different per-layer cache-group assignments on P and D | Rejected at handshake |
| PP1 | Existing support and restrictions are retained |

Shared allocations across HMA groups are not inherently block-outermost packed
layouts. HMA-required is determined from actual cache specs and manager state,
not the HMA flag alone. Push retains its separate restrictions: HMA requires
equal P/D block sizes; attention-HMA PP push rejects D TP>P TP; packed PP push
requires MLA. Usage, compatibility and push-design documentation are updated.

## Validation

Tested runtime source: HEAD `82e2045b26`. Local validation used eight NVIDIA H20 GPUs, Python 3.12.13, Torch 2.14.0+cu132, NIXL 1.5.2, FlashInfer 0.7.3 and lm-eval 0.4.12.
Precompiled extensions came from official build `11ddd587eb`.

### Unit tests

**874 passed, 2 existing ROCm-only skips, 1 existing strict xfail (#64661)**
The four-file subtotal is included in the total.
Coverage includes per-stage layer/group mapping, shared-region geometry,
notify-only/full-hit behavior, lifecycle failures and aggregation, configuration
guards, TP mapping and the upstream DCP draft-group regressions.

From the vLLM repository root with the test environment active:

```bash

  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py \

commits.pr_title: [DeepSeek-V4] Warm the DeepGEMM kernels DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 JIT-compile at runtime
commits.pr_body:
In summary, deepseek failed to warm up some kernels, which triggers JIT compilation in the inference will harm the quality. It has very **strong impact for production deepseek serving usecase**, because we don't want any JIT compile when actually serving a customer.

## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 JIT-compile several DeepGEMM kernels on live requests. Under DP + EP every rank waits for the compiling rank, so a few of these in one step exceed VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (300 s). That raises RPC call to sample_tokens timed out → EngineDeadError, the symptom reported in #41530.

## Detailed purpose
This PR warms the kernels that were missed:

1. The o_proj einsum (fp8_einsum("bhr,hdr->bhd")) was never warmed. wo_a is an is_bmm linear, so DeepGemmFp8BlockScaledMMKernel deliberately does not register it as an fp8_gemm_nt warmup provider, and deep_gemm_warmup covered only fp8_gemm_nt, the grouped contiguous GEMM and Mega-MoE.
M values. relax samples every M % 16 == 1 on top of the existing boundary heuristic. M reaches DeepGEMM's config choice only through ceil_div(M, block_m) and the m <= 16/32/64 thresholds. Every block_m enumerated for a Batched einsum is a multiple of 16 (SM100's swap-A/B branch steps in 16s), so a config can only change at M % 16 == 1. The previous sampling modelled SM90's [64, 128, 256] list and missed BLOCK_M=48/112 on SM100; @adenzhou1350 reproduced the same two on B300.
V4.1 mega attention with FP8 output is a different kernel (FP8QuantizationEpilogue, use_128x4_sfd_layout=True). The warmup carries quantize_output in its data and cache key and builds that layout.
2. The mHC prenorm GEMM's DeepGEMM path (tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm) was never warmed. The JIT registry warmed only the TileLang kernel it replaces when DeepGEMM is available.
The kernel instantiates on (n, k, num_splits, ...) and M is a launch argument, so one compile per reachable split count covers every M.
It is a VllmJitKernel (HCPrenormGemmKernel, kernels/mhc/warmup.py). Each model registers it next to its own mHC warmup, with the split function its forward pass uses: V4 passes compute_mhc_num_splits (raw compute_num_split, now also what _hc_prenorm_gemm_outputs calls); V4.1 passes compute_mhc_pre_num_splits (1/4/16 rounding).
The token bound is what one rank sees: cdiv(max_num_batched_tokens, tp) under sequence parallel, since mHC runs on the sp_shard.
The broadcast weight (k = hidden_size) is registered only on layer 0 of the first PP rank.
So split selection lives in one place per model, and neither model warms a split it cannot reach.
3. Draft kernel warm up is not contained in this scope.


To better understand why the missing happens in the swap case, I put up a diagram illustrating why this would happen. It is like we want to cover missed shape for **swap** case. Following diagram illustrates how shapes are missing for the kernel.
```
The old 218-value M set has these points between 32 and 512 -- and two real holes:

M:  32   64        128  152   192        256    304 320    384         448 456    512
    |    |          |    |     |          |      |   |      |           |   |      |
----+----+----------+----+-----+----------+------+---+------+-----------+---+------+---->
         \__ hole __/            \_ hole _/
          65..127                 193..255

config staircase (steps start only at M % 16 == 1; K@x = config first seen at M=x):

    K@1   K@33  K@65   K@97  K@129 K@161 K@193  K@225 ...
    |-----|-----|------|-----|-----|-----|------|-----|---->
                   ^                        ^
                   |                        |
            BLOCK_M=48               BLOCK_M=112
            swap_ab=true             swap_ab=true
            selected only inside     selected only inside
            the hole                 the hole
                   \________________________/
                              |
                     never compiled at startup
                     ──> compiled on a live request

Root cause: the warmup models block_ms = [64, 128, 256] -- SM90's candidate list --
so it only ever emits multiples of 64 plus wave boundaries.

   what the old model assumes:   64 -------- 128 -------- 256
   what SM100 swap-A/B does:   16 32 48 64 80 96 112 128 144 ... 256
                                     ^           ^
                                   the two that were missed

Why only the swap branch is 16-granular:

   no swap:  MMA's M = block_m  ──> coarse, only 32/64/128
      swap:  D^T = B^T * A^T, so MMA's N = block_m  ──> 16-granular,
             capped at 256 by TMEM's 512 columns
             (in code: umma_n = swap_ab ? block_m : block_n)
```


## Test Plan

1. Unit tests (CPU): `tests/model_executor/test_deep_gemm_warmup.py`, `tests/model_executor/test_mhc_prenorm_gemm_warmup.py`.
2. Kernel-level, on each GPU: compile the prenorm warmup keys into an empty `DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR`, then call `tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` for every M in 1..16384 with each model's runtime split function and count new compiles; check numerics against an fp32 reference.
3. End-to-end `vllm serve`, previous revision vs this one, one empty `DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR` per run, default config (CUDA graphs on). Snapshot committed cache entries at `/health`, then send one prefill every 32 tokens from 1 to 16384 (concurrency 1, then 16; 1,026 requests) and snapshot again. New entries are compiles that hit a live request.

Environment: the exact merge-base wheel `0.34.0rc1.dev144+g68776b023` plus this PR's files, with the md5 of every overlaid base file checked against the merge-base. Each run used a dedicated MLP pod (4 × GB200 SM100, 152 SMs, nvcc 13.1; 8 × H100 SM90, nvcc 13.0) with no foreign GPU processes before or after. Settings: `VLLM_DEEP_GEMM_WARMUP=relax`, `VLLM_BLOCKSCALE_FP8_GEMM_FLASHINFER=0`, `--max-model-len 20480`.

## Test Result

1. `pytest test_deep_gemm_warmup.py test_mhc_prenorm_gemm_warmup.py`: **25 passed**.

2. Prenorm kernel-level (max_tokens 16384, both weight shapes):

| GPU | model | previous revision compiles | this PR compiles | new compiles during M = 1..16384 sweep |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GB200 | V4.1 | 37 (31 never used by V4.1) | **6** | **0** |
| GB200 | V4 | 37 | 37 | **0** |
| H100 | V4.1 | 36 (30 never used) | **6** | **0** |
| H100 | V4 | 36 | 36 | **0** |

   On one GB200 process, compiling the V4.1 set took 68.4 s before and 11.2 s now.

3. End-to-end:

| GPU | model / parallelism | revision | prenorm kernels at `/health` | runtime DeepGEMM JIT during traffic | errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GB200 | V4.1-Flash TP4 + EP | previous (×2) | 40, 40 | 0, 0 | 0 |
| GB200 | V4.1-Flash TP4 + EP | this PR (×3) | **6**, 6, 6 | **0**, 0, 0 | 0 |
| GB200 | V4-Flash DP4 + EP | previous / this | 37 / 37 | 0 / 0 | 0 |
| GB200 | V4-Flash TP4 + EP | previous / this | 37 / 37 | 0 / 0 | 0 |
| GB200 | V4-Flash TP4 + EP + Mega-MoE (SP) | previous / this | 37 / **35** | 0 / **0** | 0 |
| H100 | V4-Flash TP8 | previous / this | 36 / 36 | 0 / 0 | 0 |

   V4.1 cold start, counting only runs whose TileLang/Triton/FlashInfer caches were already warm (only the DeepGEMM cache was emptied):

This PR helps reducing the deepgemm warm up times

| | DeepGEMM warmup | time-to-ready |
|---|---|---|
| previous revision | 118 s, 130 s | 390 s, 381 s |
| this PR | 52 s, 52 s | 310 s, 320 s |

   The first run on a pod (1333 s) also pays those other caches, so it is excluded from the comparison.

   Earlier measurement with the DeepGEMM warmup disabled (vLLM 0.33 nightly, eager on GB200): 34 runtime compiles on H100 TP8 (21 fp8 GEMM, 12 prenorm, 1 indexer) and 78 on GB200 TP4 (52 fp8/fp4 GEMM, 17 prenorm, 9 einsum).


### scope not covered
sm90_fp8_mqa_logits (indexer): one compile per indexer shape at the first call on SM90, since its key has no M. Not warmed, because logits_dtype is part of the key and is not discoverable from the module; guessing it would warm a kernel that never runs.
No spec-decode run, so the draft-model change is verified from source and unit tests only.
The prenorm warmup now follows kernel_config.enable_jit_warmup (like the other mHC warmups) rather than VLLM_DEEP_GEMM_WARMUP.

commits.pr_title: [Transformers backend] Default decoder pooling to LAST and honour `is_causal=False`
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes for Qwen2 embedding models on the Transformers modeling backend: decoder pooling models now default to `LAST` pooling, and `is_causal=False` in the config now makes them bidirectional. The default-pooling fix is extracted from #59206 and the `is_causal` fix from #67018, so #66821 (Qwen2 port) does not have to wait for either. Tracked in #67003.

## Claims

- Text-only backend pooling models default to `CLS` if the HF model (built on the meta device) has a bidirectional attention layer, and `LAST` otherwise, as native models do. Before, every backend pooling model defaulted to `CLS`, which also made decoders `encoder_only` and disabled prefix caching and chunked prefill.
- The backend now honours `is_causal=False` in the text config when it picks the attention class, multimodal models included. HF's Qwen2 and Llama attention hardcode `is_causal=True`, so on the backend gte-Qwen2 ran causal attention.
- Trade-off: the pooling probe builds the HF model during `ModelConfig` init, so for `trust_remote_code` models remote code now runs there as well.

## Validation

B200, `main` vs this PR, native (`--model-impl vllm`) vs backend (`--model-impl transformers`) embeddings of the same 4 prompts:

```text
# main
vllm Qwen2Model LAST decoder
transformers TransformersEmbeddingModel CLS encoder_only
COSINE Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct [0.19643, 0.23489, 0.55864, 0.35244]
vllm Qwen2ForCausalLM LAST encoder_only
transformers TransformersForCausalLM LAST encoder_only
COSINE Alibaba-NLP/gte-Qwen2-1.5B-instruct [0.59729, 0.62796, 0.54614, 0.73009]

# this PR
vllm Qwen2Model LAST decoder
transformers TransformersEmbeddingModel LAST decoder
COSINE Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct [1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0]
vllm Qwen2ForCausalLM LAST encoder_only
transformers TransformersForCausalLM LAST encoder_only
COSINE Alibaba-NLP/gte-Qwen2-1.5B-instruct [1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0]
```

from vllm import LLM

           "The mitochondria is the powerhouse of the cell.", "def add(a, b): return a + b"]

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Run the nightly Python 3.14 smoke test on AMD
commits.pr_body:
- `python_only_compile.sh`: when `PYTHON_ONLY_COMPILE_PYTHON` is set on ROCm, build a fresh uv venv with that Python, install the image's exact torch/torchvision ROCm builds from TheRock for the detected GPU arch, then `uv pip install -e .` against the same-build precompiled wheel
- `python_only_compile.sh`: run the smoke generation with the venv's own ROCm SDK and amdsmi bindings instead of the image's
- `misc.yaml`: add a `mirror.amd` (MI355, 55 min, same as the neighbouring Python-only Installation mirror) to `[Nightly] Python 3.14 Smoke`

The NVIDIA `[Nightly] Python 3.14 Smoke` step had no AMD counterpart, and the script's ROCm path ignored `PYTHON_ONLY_COMPILE_PYTHON`: it always ran `setup.py develop` into the image's Python 3.12, so a plain mirror fails the script's own version check with `AssertionError: expected Python 3.14, got 3.12`. The new branch mirrors what the CUDA branch does with `--torch-backend`, but pulls torch from TheRock's index since it publishes the image's ROCm builds for every supported Python. This depends on #66313 (tensorizer 2.10.1 -> 2.12.1): on 3.14, tensorizer 2.10.1 fails at import with `KeyError: 'crypto_stream_salsa20_NONCEBYTES'` (PEP 649), and since the model loader imports it, `LLM()` dies. It has to land first or together with this. #65313 renames this step to `[Nightly] Python 3.12 Smoke` once 3.14 becomes the image default, so whichever PR lands second carries the mirror over to the renamed step. No open PR adds an AMD mirror for this step or touches the ROCm path of `python_only_compile.sh` (searched open PRs for `python_only_compile`, `PYTHON_ONLY_COMPILE_PYTHON`, `Python 3.14 Smoke`, `python-314-smoke`, `ROCm python 3.14`, `python-only rocm`).

commits.pr_title: [EPLB] Support heterogeneous DeepSeek V4/V4.1 DSpark draft experts
commits.pr_body:
## Overview
Follow-up of #57549

Enable EPLB for DeepSeek V4 and V4.1 DSpark drafts when their expert topology differs from the target model.
This PR covers DSpark’s draft model loader.
Related: [#59611](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59611) fixes redundant expert loading in the target model. 
Open #66045 addresses draft expert filtering during weight loading; it is complementary and does not implement heterogeneous EPLB state or load balancing.

## Claims

- Register supported DSpark draft MoE models with the target's EPLB state and reduce their load statistics together, including when their physical expert counts differ.
- When draft R is unset and the routed-count sets match, inherit the resolved target R if it is valid for the draft. If the sets differ, compute the draft minimum.
- Honor an explicit draft R when it is valid for every draft routed count. Reject an invalid explicit value and suggest the minimum valid count when one count works for every draft layer.
- Read `draft_num_redundant_experts` from `--eplb-config`, alongside the target EPLB settings. `draft_enable_eplb` remains in `--speculative-config`.
- Enable EPLB by default for supported V4.1 DSpark drafts when target EPLB is enabled. A DSpark draft with `draft_tensor_parallel_size=1` requires prefill context parallelism or data parallelism greater than 1; otherwise, config validation rejects it. DSpark draft EPLB is incompatible with Elastic EP; set `draft_enable_eplb=false` to disable it.
- Include redundant physical slots in V4.1 DSpark's fused-MoE weight mapping.

## Validation

### GSM8K validation.

server:
```
/home/ilmarkov/vllm_venv/bin/vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --port 8000 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --served-model-name deepseek-v41-flash \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --enable-eplb \
  --eplb-config '{"num_redundant_experts":4,"step_interval":100,"log_balancedness":true}' \
  --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41 \
  --sparse-indexer-topk-backend flashinfer \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5}'
```

client:
```
python \
  tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py \
  --num-questions 1319 \
  --num-shots 5 \
  --max-tokens 256 \
  --host http://127.0.0.1 \
  --port 8000 \
  --temperature 0.0 \
  --seed 42 \
```

Result. Accuracy: 0.902 (1,319 questions, 5-shot); invalid responses: 0.

Startup and rearrangement logs from the GSM8K run (target R=4, automatically selected draft R=0):

    `(APIServer pid=1698551) INFO 11-06 13:13:46 [startup.py:96] non-default args: {'model_tag': 'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash', 'model': 'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash', 'tokenizer_mode': 'deepseek_v41', 'trust_remote_code': True, 'max_model_len': 8192, 'served_model_name': ['deepseek-v41-flash'], 'attention_backend': 'FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41', 'tensor_parallel_size': 4, 'enable_expert_parallel': True, 'enable_eplb': True, 'eplb_config': EPLBConfig(window_size=1000, step_interval=100, num_redundant_experts=4, draft_num_redundant_experts=None, log_balancedness=True, log_balancedness_interval=1, use_async=True, policy='default', communicator=None, enable_migration_batching=False), 'gpu_memory_utilization': 0.9, 'kv_cache_dtype': 'fp8', 'sparse_indexer_topk_backend': 'flashinfer', 'speculative_config': {'method': 'dspark', 'num_speculative_tokens': 5}}`
    `(APIServer pid=1698551) INFO 11-06 13:13:50 [speculative.py:1745] Draft EPLB redundant expert count not specified, defaulting to minimum valid value: 0 (routed_expert_counts=(128,), ep_size=4)`
    `(Worker_TP0_EP0 pid=1702148) INFO 11-06 13:17:00 [eplb_utils.py:149] EPLB is enabled for MoE part of drafter model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.`
    `(Worker_TP0_EP0 pid=1702148) INFO 11-06 13:17:01 [eplb_utils.py:171] EPLB is enabled for MoE part of model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.`
    `(Worker_TP0_EP0 pid=1702148) INFO 11-06 13:17:10 [eplb_state.py:798] Rearranging experts (async mode) (profile)...`
    `(Worker_TP0_EP0 pid=1702148) INFO 11-06 13:17:12 [eplb_state.py:968] Rearranged experts  (profile)  in 1.76 s.`
    `(Worker_TP0_EP0 pid=1702148) INFO 11-06 13:17:12 [eplb_state.py:968] Rearranged experts  (profile)  in 1.81 s.`
    `(Worker_TP0_EP0 pid=1702148) INFO 11-06 13:20:38 [eplb_state.py:694] EPLB step: 98 for model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (draft): avg_tokens=4500.00, max_tokens=6896, balancedness=0.6526, steps until the next rearrangement: 2`
    `(Worker_TP0_EP0 pid=1702148) INFO 11-06 13:20:38 [eplb_state.py:694] EPLB step: 98 for model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: avg_tokens=235080.00, max_tokens=316436, balancedness=0.7429, steps until the next rearrangement: 2`
    `(Worker_TP0_EP0 pid=1702148) INFO 11-06 13:20:38 [eplb_state.py:798] Rearranging experts (async mode) ...`
    `(Worker_TP0_EP0 pid=1702148) INFO 11-06 13:20:38 [eplb_state.py:694] EPLB step: 99 for model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (draft): avg_tokens=4500.00, max_tokens=6764, balancedness=0.6653, steps until the next rearrangement: 1`
    `(Worker_TP0_EP0 pid=1702148) INFO 11-06 13:20:38 [eplb_state.py:694] EPLB step: 99 for model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: avg_tokens=512400.00, max_tokens=682868, balancedness=0.7504, steps until the next rearrangement: 1`

Both models (target and draft) are involved in eplb rearrangement.


## Details

The target and DSpark draft can have different routed and physical expert counts. EPLB state now keeps topology-dependent counts per registered model and handles load-stat reductions when models have different physical expert dimensions.

For supported MoE drafts, draft EPLB is enabled by default whenever target EPLB is enabled. Set `speculative_config.draft_enable_eplb=false` to disable it for the draft while leaving target EPLB enabled. DeepSeek V4 and V4.1 DSpark drafts require the draft EP group to have more than one rank when draft EPLB is enabled; `draft_tensor_parallel_size=1` is rejected when prefill context parallelism and data parallelism are both 1. Draft EPLB for DSpark is rejected with Elastic EP during config validation, with a suggestion to disable draft EPLB.

DSpark’s custom weight loader is a separate call path from the target model’s `get_expert_mapping`. Since DSpark is now registered with EPLB, its redundant physical slots must also receive the replicated expert weights. #59611 addresses the target model’s mapping; end-to-end use with redundant experts requires that fix as well.


The PR example adds `draft_num_redundant_experts` in `--eplb-config`. The value is a draft override and does not change the target's `num_redundant_experts`. It is only consumed when a speculative MoE draft is configured; without one, the draft-specific setting is ignored.

Draft R resolution follows three cases. 
 - With no draft override and matching target/draft routed-count sets, inherit the target R when it is already resolved and valid for the draft. 
 - With no override and different routed-count sets, compute the minimum valid draft R. 
 - For an explicit draft R, use it if it satisfies divisibility for every draft routed count; otherwise, fail config validation and suggest the minimum valid R when one value works for all layers. 
 - If draft layers require different padding values, validation reports that no single R works. 
 - When target R is automatic but still unresolved during draft validation, matching topologies compute the same minimum independently; target R is stored later by the normal `VllmConfig` path.

For target EPLB validation, an unset target R is now resolved locally for the divisibility check without mutating `EPLBConfig`; this lets ngram configurations reach the normal `VllmConfig` path that resolves the target count.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Fix KV cache pages for hybrid models with draft layers
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

This PR fixes how vLLM picks KV cache pages when a model mixes layer types, which is what speculative decoding with a draft model on a hybrid (attention plus linear-attention) target does. FlashInfer now chooses kernel pages per layer, padded manager pages can split into kernel pages, and hybrid block alignment counts the drafter's KV. It is independent of #62961, #62962, #62963 and #62964, and of #63279, which carries the FA4 dense warmup coverage that started in this PR.

## Claims

- FlashInfer kernel pages follow each attention group's own head counts, with query heads from its layers and KV heads from its spec. An MHA draft layer next to a GQA target otherwise gets the target's large pages, and its metadata builder rejects them at startup. `AttentionBackend.get_supported_kernel_block_sizes_for_layers(kv_cache_spec, layer_names)` carries this and defaults to `get_supported_kernel_block_sizes`. The model runner and the NIXL and Mooncake connectors pass each group's layer names, so P/D transfer uses the same kernel blocks as the runner.
- A padded manager page splits into uniformly strided kernel pages, and manager-page boundaries are kept. Interleaved layers and non-divisible padding still fail with a clear error.
- Hybrid block alignment includes the drafter's KV bytes per token. When a draft has more KV per token than the target, it sets the common page size, and every recurrent-state page is padded up to it. For a 64-layer Qwen3.5-style GDN model with a one-layer draft that is a 5.2x padding, and the KV pool holds about 61 concurrent requests of 2.5k tokens.

## Validation

AI assistance (Claude) was used to prepare this change; I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests listed below.

The changed test files cover per-layer head counts and connector grouping, the attention utilities, the kernel block selection and the GPU model runner. I broke the head-count fix on purpose to check that a test catches it. On B300, making FlashInfer ignore the layer's heads fails the MHA-draft case.

On CPU (`VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`, one pytest process per file), I ran the attention, KV-cache, spec-decode and worker files this PR touches or depends on.

| Build | Files | Passed | Failed | Skipped |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `main` (`98468d0f66`) | 84 | 1335 | 143 | 957 |
| this PR | 84 | 1347 | 143 | 961 |

The 84 files include the NIXL and Mooncake connector tests. The 143 failures, and 35 errors at collection, are the same cases on both builds, and `pre-commit` passes on the range.

On B300 with FlashInfer installed, the FlashInfer and connector cases in `test_group_head_counts.py` pass (5 of 5), and `test_attn_utils.py` passes 62 of 62.

I served Qwen3.8-27B at TP4 on 4x B300 with this PR on `main` (`98468d0f66`), with the default attention backend (FlashInfer), `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` and `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, with 33 SPEED-Bench prompts (greedy, 384 tokens each). The server logged no GPU-sync errors. At batch 1 the outputs are bitwise identical to `main` (33 of 33) and decode speed matches (226.8 tok/s against 226.0, one server each). At 16 concurrent, two servers of `main` itself agree on 22 of 33 outputs on this base, so equality there is not a usable check. This PR against `main` gives 23 of 33 in the same job, which is within that spread.

End to end, a chain speculator with an MHA draft on a GQA hybrid target starts with the default attention backend, where without this PR it starts only when forced to `FLASH_ATTN`, and it serves concurrent and mid-prefill (16k-token) requests. A TP8 hybrid target with a draft serves 20 of 20 requests within the near-tie criterion against no speculation. I ran these two on the previous base (`56e67b46a3`), before the head-count fix moved from the cache spec to the backend method.

```bash
pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_group_head_counts.py tests/v1/attention/test_kpool_indexer_block_sizes.py tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py
python -m pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_group_head_counts.py tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py   # on B300
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B --tensor-parallel-size 4 --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 16 --no-enable-prefix-caching
```

## Not a duplicate

I ran the duplicate-work searches from `AGENTS.md` §1 (open PRs, with keywords on kernel block size, padded pages, hybrid drafter block size and Mamba page padding). They found related work, and none of it makes the same fix. This PR uses no code from them.

- #58630 passes each layer's KV spec into kernel block-size selection. This PR adds the layer names that the FlashInfer check needs next to that spec, so the two are complementary.
- #60252 and #58207 change how a hybrid model picks its group or block size. They leave the drafter's KV out of the alignment.
- #59297 (draft) moves kernel-block mapping into each attention group, with a per-group kernel-block stride. It is a larger refactor of the mapping that the padded-page split here relies on, and if it lands first, the split here becomes a stride choice in its mapping.
- #50169 fixes KV allocation for sliding-window drafters. This PR fixes the page alignment that a full-attention drafter on a hybrid target forces.

## Includes and credits

This PR contains no code from other open PRs.

## Details

- Query heads stay out of the cache spec, which describes only the KV cache layout (as in #53002). FlashInfer reads them from the group's layers when kernel blocks are chosen at KV cache initialization. Callers without layer names, and calls with no current config, keep the model-wide answer, so other models pick the same pages as before.
- The alignment change builds a fresh spec for the draft, so the draft does not inherit the target's value-head dimension. Speculative-state reservations are unchanged.
- All GPU measurements are on B300.
